commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Use fused PLE Triton kernels on the AMD backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Ports the fused Qwen4Exp PLE Triton kernels from [#54517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54517) (with the [#55375](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55375) stride fix) to the AMD backend, which still runs the older PyTorch PLE path. Follows up on [#54764](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54764); supersedes [#58325](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58325).

## Claims

- Output throughput on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MXFP4, TP2 on MI355X, rises by +1.2% to +2.6% at each serving point (geomean +1.7%, +2.2% and +1.6% over three repeats). GSM8K is unchanged within noise.
- Per decode step, the PLE layer drops from 19 kernel launches to 3.
- The AMD backend no longer builds padded `[num_reqs, max_len]` n-gram buffers.
- NVIDIA and AMD now share one PLE kernel module. Net −360 non-test lines (+226 / −586).

## Validation

**Unit tests.** MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-18f8f96025` with this branch's `vllm/models/qwen4_exp` and `tests/models/qwen4_exp` mounted (the nightly and this branch's base have no other differences in that package):

```text
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py
90 passed, 15 warnings in 27.71s
```

- `test_fused_conv_correctness` now also runs on `amd.ple_layer.Qwen4ExpPLELayer`, covering every decode, prefill, spec and mixed case and both conv-state layouts.
- New `test_amd_ngram_embedding_matches_reference_under_compile` checks the AMD n-gram embedding under `torch.compile(fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` against the Python reference, including an empty request and EOS in the context.

**End to end.** `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`, TP2 on MI355X. Control and candidate are the same ROCm image, with and without this change. Mean of 3 repeats, control → this change:

| ISL / OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Per repeat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k | 4 | 537.5 → 551.4 (+2.6%) | 6.82 → 6.64 | +2.1%, +3.0%, +2.7% |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 1,277.3 → 1,301.1 (+1.9%) | 11.35 → 11.16 | +1.6%, +2.5%, +1.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 2,296.3 → 2,336.0 (+1.7%) | 24.48 → 24.04 | +1.6%, +2.1%, +1.6% |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 231.1 → 233.7 (+1.2%) | 10.49 → 10.39 | +1.7%, +1.0%, +0.8% |

GSM8K (5-shot, chat template, 1,319 questions, flexible-extract): 0.9639 → 0.9624 (mean of 3). **No regressions.**

| Repeat | Control → this change | Fixed / broken | Exact McNemar p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0.9659 → 0.9598 | 11 / 19 | 0.20 |
| 2 | 0.9629 → 0.9629 | 18 / 18 | 1.00 |
| 3 | 0.9629 → 0.9644 | 18 / 16 | 0.86 |

**Decode trace.** Torch profiler on rank 0, 8k/128 at c16, 128 decode steps per arm:

| | Control | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PLE kernel launches per step | 19 | 3 (`_ple_ngram_ids`, `_ple_gate`, `_ple_conv`) |
| PLE GPU time per step | 134 µs | 18 µs |
| Decode step | 10.45 ms | 10.22 ms (−2.2%) |

**Reproduce:**

```bash
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --port 8000

# per point: (ISL, OSL, conc, prompts) = (8192,1024,4,32) (8192,1024,16,64) (8192,1024,64,128) (60000,600,4,16)
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --port 8000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 64 --warmup-requests 16 --request-rate inf

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_gen_toks=2048 \
  --seed 4321 --log_samples --output_path gsm8k-out
```

## Details

**Why the kernels port unchanged.** They are plain Triton. Their PDL path is gated on `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`, which is false on ROCm, so `nvidia/ops/ple.py` moves to `common/ops/ple.py` as is, with the NVIDIA imports updated.

**AMD model changes:**

- **`Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding`:** calls `ple_ngram_ids` instead of building padded buffers with gathers, a shift and a scatter, and drops the `max_num_reqs` argument. The pinned-host and device embedding lookups that follow are unchanged.
- **`Qwen4ExpPLELayer`:**
  - `key_proj` and `value_proj` become one replicated `MergedColumnParallelLinear` named `kv_proj` (`disable_tp=True`, as on NVIDIA).
  - The gate is `ple_gate`.
  - The short conv is `ple_conv`, which replaces the separate decode, prefill and spec `F.conv1d` branches with NVIDIA's single dispatch.
  - `qwen4_exp_ple_short_conv` stays a splitting op.
- **Residual:** the fused conv also adds the decoder layer's residual, so `Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer` now assigns `hidden_states = self.ple(...)` instead of adding the PLE output itself.
- **Weight loading:**
  - `ple.key_proj` and `ple.value_proj` map onto the two `kv_proj` shards.
  - `_HC_WEIGHTS_MAPPER` becomes `_EXTRA_WEIGHTS_MAPPER`, since it now also maps PLE weights.
  - `kv_proj` is added to `packed_modules_mapping`, so a quantization exclude list that names the original projections still applies. The Quark MXFP4 checkpoint keeps both in BF16.
  - The AMD MTP draft runs without PLE, so it only picks up the mapper rename.

**Design choice: a custom op around `ple_ngram_ids` on AMD.** Unlike the NVIDIA path, the AMD model runs the n-gram embedding inside `torch.compile`, where `query_start_loc` has a dynamic leading dimension. The kernel's launch grid comes from the request count, which Dynamo would otherwise trace symbolically. So the call goes through a small opaque op, `qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_ids`. The new compile test covers that path.

> Validated on MI355X (gfx950) only, not MI300X/MI325X (gfx942). The kernels contain no architecture-specific code.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't int-sort attention-type names in --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers for packed KV dtypes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` accepts layer indices or attention type names like `sliding_window`, but with a `turboquant_*` or `ultraquant_4bit` cache dtype, `create_engine_config` sorts the merged skip list with `key=int` and crashes on any name.

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers sliding_window` (and the same with `ultraquant_4bit`) no longer fails with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'sliding_window'`.
- Index-only skip lists hold the same layers as before. They are now ordered as strings (`"10"` before `"5"`), so a list with two-digit indices gets a different `CacheConfig` hash once, i.e. one compile-cache miss after upgrading.

## Validation

Reproduced at config level, platform forced to CPU (no kernels involved; I don't have a CUDA box):

```python
EngineArgs(model="facebook/opt-125m", kv_cache_dtype="turboquant_4bit_nc",
           kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers=["sliding_window", "5"]).create_engine_config()
# main:        ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'sliding_window'
# this branch: skip list ['0', '1', '10', '11', '5', 'sliding_window']
```

Same result with `ultraquant_4bit`. No test added: per review, the field is typed `list[str]`, so the int sort key shouldn't come back. `pre-commit` passes on the changed file.

End to end, I hit this on ROCm (gfx1201) with a hybrid GDN target and a DFlash2 drafter: TurboQuant gets picked for the target's full-attention layers, and the drafter's sliding-window layers have no TurboQuant backend, so skipping `sliding_window` is the documented way out. With the same fix applied to our ROCm build, the engine gets past config.

## Details

The user's list can hold names, but the merge with TurboQuant's boundary layers (always indices) sorted everything as ints. Now the merged list is sorted as strings. The sort stays because the list is a `CacheConfig.compute_hash()` factor and is built from a set, so without it the order (and the hash) would vary with `PYTHONHASHSEED`. Order doesn't change behaviour, since `Attention` matches entries as strings.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this sort. #54599 mentions the `sliding_window` case not working with TurboQuant "for a different reason" but doesn't change it, and #59178 / #60252 / #60023 touch the same flag in other places.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change. I reviewed the diff and ran the reproduction above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't warn about missing watermark config for default requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #56801, every engine started without `--watermark-config` logs "Watermarking is enabled for this request, but the engine has no watermark configuration..." on its first request, although nothing asked for watermarking ([reported here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56801#issuecomment-6032728937)). This PR keeps that warning only for requests that set `watermarking=True`.

## Claims

- On an engine without a watermark config, default requests (`watermarking` unset) no longer log the warning.
- `watermarking=True` on such an engine still warns once and runs without a watermark.
- The greedy, beam search, and trace replay fallback warnings on engines with a watermark config are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/watermarking/` (1x H200): 184 passed, 3 skipped (the skipped tests need 2 GPUs). `tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py`, `tests/test_sampling_params.py` and `tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py`: 82 passed.
- CI: `tests/watermarking` already runs in the "(CPU) V1 Others" Buildkite step, which triggers on `vllm/config/`.
- With the old condition restored, the updated `test_requests_without_engine_config_are_unwatermarked` fails for all 3 of its cases.
- Offline `LLM.generate` with Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and no watermark config. Before (main c83935b300): one warning on the first default request. After: no warning for default sampling, default greedy, or `watermarking=False`. One warning for `watermarking=True`.
- `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` plus `/v1/completions`. Before (merged #56801 code, same condition as main): one warning after a default request. After: none for a default request, one for `"watermarking": true`.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

Root cause: the branch of `VllmConfig._check_supports_watermarking` for engines without a watermark config tested `config.watermarking is not False`, so the default `None` also warned. It now tests `is True`. The docs already say watermarking is disabled when `--watermark-config` is omitted, so no docs change is needed.

The test changes update the two assertions that expected a warning for default requests on an engine without a config. They also add a plain `SamplingParams()` case to the existing test for such requests.

The Rust frontend sets `watermarking=true` before the engine and does not go through this check, so it is unaffected.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Scope deprecated CLI argument warnings to the parser that defines them
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #48094 (also reported earlier as #42852). On Python 3.10–3.12, `vllm chat` and `vllm complete` print a spurious `argument 'url' is deprecated` warning on every run, because `run-batch`'s deprecated `--url` leaks into sibling subcommands.

cc @hmellor

## Claims

- `vllm chat` / `vllm complete` no longer warn that their own (valid) `--url` is deprecated.
- Deprecated arguments still warn for the subcommand that defines them (`vllm run-batch --url ...` still warns once).
- Each parser now only checks its own deprecated arguments, so the same leak can't happen for future deprecated arguments, and the top-level parser no longer re-checks a subcommand's arguments.

## Validation

Python 3.12.3 (WSL2 Ubuntu), editable install with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

New regression test `test_deprecated_arg_scoped_to_subcommand`:

```
pytest tests/utils_/test_argparse_utils.py -k deprecated   # on main: 1 failed
pytest tests/utils_/test_argparse_utils.py                 # with this PR: 24 passed
```

End-to-end, counting `argument 'url' is deprecated` lines (no server or GPU needed):

| Command | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm chat --url http://127.0.0.1:9/v1` | 1 | 0 |
| `vllm complete --url http://127.0.0.1:9/v1` | 1 | 0 |
| `vllm run-batch -i x.jsonl -o y.jsonl --model facebook/opt-125m --url 1.2.3.4` | 1 | 1 |

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>` (ruff, mypy 3.10–3.13, etc.) pass.

## Details

**Root cause.** Below Python 3.13, `FlexibleArgumentParser` emulates `add_argument(..., deprecated=True)` by recording the action in `_deprecated`, a set defined on the class and therefore shared by every parser and subparser. `parse_known_args` then walks that whole set. `run-batch` marks its `--url` (default `0.0.0.0`) as deprecated via `frontend_kwargs["url"]["deprecated"] = True`, and since `vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py` builds every subcommand's parser on each invocation, that action is always in the set. When `chat`/`complete` parse their own `--url` (default `http://localhost:8000/v1`), the value never equals run-batch's default, so the warning fires. (This is also why a grep for `deprecated=True` doesn't find it.)

**Fix.** Make `_deprecated` an instance variable. It is created at the top of `__init__`, because `ArgumentParser.__init__` already adds argument groups and `-h`, and `_FlexibleArgumentGroup` shares its parser's set, because argparse groups don't keep a reference to their container. `_SubParsersAction` calls each subparser's own `parse_known_args`, so a subcommand's deprecated arguments are only checked when that subcommand is parsed. The warning condition (value differs from the default) is unchanged. Python 3.13+ is unaffected since it uses argparse's native support.

**Prior work.** #42854 proposed the same per-instance fix but was auto-closed as stale without a review. No other open PR addresses this issue.

AI-assisted; I reviewed and tested all changes.

---

commits.pr_title: [Compile] Remove torch.compile-based sequence parallelism and AsyncTP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Remove the torch.compile-based sequence parallelism pass (`SequenceParallelismPass`) and the AsyncTP pass (`AsyncTPPass`) that is built on top of it. This feature is not supported in Model Runner V2, and we are reducing our reliance on torch.compile. Manual (model-level) sequence parallelism under `vllm/models/` is unaffected.

Supersedes open work that extends compile-based SP/AsyncTP: #36851, #37489, #38151.

## Claims

- Deletes `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/sequence_parallelism.py` and `collective_fusion.py` (AsyncTP only ever ran after the SP rewrite, so without SP it matches nothing).
- Removes `PassConfig.enable_sp`, `fuse_gemm_comms`, and `sp_min_token_num`, plus all SP-only plumbing:
  - config: O2/O3 defaults, SP auto-enable and threshold, the SP compile-range endpoint, forced `splitting_ops=[]`/FULL cudagraph, TP-divisible cudagraph capture sizes, the batch-invariance override, and the MRV2 unsupported-feature entry;
  - MRV1 runner/worker: padding `num_tokens` to a multiple of TP, `is_residual_scattered_for_sp`, and the residual all-gather on PP send/recv;
  - `resolve_cudagraph_mode_and_sizes` / `adjust_cudagraph_sizes_for_spec_decode` drop their now-unused `tensor_parallel_size` argument;
  - unused FlashInfer `*_mm_out` helpers that only AsyncTP used.
- Deletes the SP/AsyncTP tests and their CI steps; updates docs (`fusions.md`, `cuda_graphs.md`, `vllm_ir.md`, `batch_invariance.md`).
- Net: +33 / −4798 lines across 34 files.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, etc.) passes.
- E2E: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with TP=2, PP=2 generates correctly on both MRV1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) and the default runner, covering the edited PP send/recv and intermediate-tensor paths.
- Unit tests (GB200):
  - `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`, `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py`: all pass.
  - `tests/compile/test_config.py`: all pass except 9 cudagraph capture-size tests, which fail the same way on `main` on this machine (unrelated).
  - Manual-SP suites still pass: `tests/models/{kimi_k3,deepseek_v32,glm5next}/test_sequence_parallel.py` and `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py` (30 passed, 1 skipped).
- No model eval: the feature was off by default (`IS_DENSE = False`), so the default execution path is unchanged.

## Details

- **Breaking config change:** `PassConfig` forbids extra fields, so passing `enable_sp`, `fuse_gemm_comms`, or `sp_min_token_num` now raises a validation error instead of being silently ignored. These were opt-in, off by default, and unsupported on MRV2.
- **Kept on purpose:** the generic `all_gather_tensors` option on `GroupCoordinator.{send,isend,recv,irecv}_tensor_dict`. Nothing passes it after this PR, but a future model that combines manual SP with PP may need it. Today, every manual-SP model gates SP on `pipeline_parallel_size == 1` (or has PP disabled), so no sharded tensors cross PP stages.
- The `vllm.reduce_scatter` / `vllm.all_gather` custom ops, compile ranges, `use_inductor_graph_partition`, and the attention-fusion `splitting_ops` logic stay, because other passes and models still use them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Check batch-invariance support for every attention backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the attention selector refuses backends that do not declare `supports_batch_invariance()` ("VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for ..."). Models that select their own attention backend never go through the selector, so they start anyway and silently return batch-dependent output. This PR applies the same check to every attention layer when the attention groups are built.

## Claims

- `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` starts in batch-invariant mode on `main` and the determinism tests report violations (for example 32 of 32 prompts). With this PR the engine refuses to start with the existing error message.
- Models on the standard backends are unaffected: the determinism tests still pass for `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8` (GB300), `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (A10). Every model on the tested list in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` uses a standard backend.
- New unit test for the check.

## Validation

GB300 runs: 4x NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), `main` at `182247257f` versus that commit plus this PR's source change. A10 runs: 2x NVIDIA A10 (SM 8.6), `main` at `d09ff77637` plus this PR's source change. One pytest process per test. The blocks are copied from the logs without editing.

**1. `main`: MiniMax-M3 runs in batch-invariant mode and is not batch invariant** (tensor-parallel 4)

```text
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN]"
E               Failed: Nondeterministic outputs detected: 5 failed out of 5 trials (max_batch_size=128).
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 532.70s (0:08:52) ==================

VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[16-16-FLASH_ATTN]"
E           Failed: Batch invariance violated in 32/32 prompts. See output above for details.
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 116.67s (0:01:56) ==================
```

**2. This PR: the engine refuses to start for MiniMax-M3 in batch-invariant mode**

```text
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[FLASH_ATTN]"
(Worker_TP2 pid=2792149) ERROR 10-06 05:23:45 [multiproc_executor.py:1058] RuntimeError: VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE_INDEXER.
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 73.05s (0:01:13) ===================
```

**3. This PR: models on the standard backends still pass**


`lm_eval` and `vllm bench serve` comparisons are not included because the change is a start-up check only: no kernel or request path is touched, and for the affected model the "after" state is that the engine does not start.

## Details

**Root cause.** `supports_batch_invariance()` is enforced in `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py`. Attention layers that set their backend themselves (the model packages under `vllm/models/`, for example MiniMax-M3's sparse attention and indexer) are not created through the selector, and none of those backends declares support, so batch-invariant mode was accepted for them without any guarantee. I found this by running the determinism suite on MiniMax-M3: it fails on `main`, and still fails with #59985 applied, so it is not the router issue fixed there.

**Change.** `init_attn_backend` already visits the backend of every attention layer; it now raises the selector's error for a backend that does not declare support when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set. Backends that do support it only need to override `supports_batch_invariance()`.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- Models with self-selected backends (MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3 and similar) now fail fast in batch-invariant mode instead of starting. None of them is on the tested list, and for the one I could test the mode did not hold.
- Only the Model Runner V2 path is changed; the equivalent loop in the V1 runner is left as is, given its deprecation.
- This does not make MiniMax-M3 batch invariant; it makes the lack of support explicit.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] RDNA3 W4A16 MoE: handle the N-first CT weight layout
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#52798 ("Use canonical N-first weight format for CT WNA16 MoE", merged
September 28) changed the layout compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE weights reach
the backends in, but the RDNA3 (gfx1100) path was not updated. Since then any
compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE checkpoint fails on RDNA3 at the first forward,
with an assertion on `w1_zp` in the experts.

Two things broke:

- `_process_weights_rdna3` still read the weights as K-first
  (`[E, K // 8, N]`, scales `[E, groups, N]`), which is what
  `moe_gptq_gemm_rdna3` needs, but they now arrive N-first
  (`[E, N, K // 8]`, scales `[E, N, groups]`).
- `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod` registered the synthesized zero points
  only for the CPU backend. The RDNA3 kernel needs them too, even for
  symmetric checkpoints (the oracle synthesizes them), so `w13/w2_qzeros`
  never reached the layer.

## What changes

- `oracle/int_wna16.py`: `_process_weights_rdna3` transposes weights and
  scales to the kernel's K-first layout before the exllama shuffle.
- `compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py`: register the synthesized zero points
  for `WNA16MoEBackend.RDNA3` as well as CPU.

Nothing changes for other backends.

## Not a duplicate

`upstream/main` (df417f780a) still has the K-first read. I searched open PRs
for `rdna3 moe`, `rdna3 w4a16`, `gfx1100 moe`, `moe_gptq_gemm_rdna3`,
`rdna3 compressed-tensors` and `52798`. The only open PR touching
`int_wna16.py` for RDNA3 is #59783, which adds a group-size check in backend
selection and does not touch weight processing.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py -v
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

- [x] A regression test, `test_process_weights_from_compressed_tensors_layout`:
  it builds weights the way compressed-tensors hands them to the oracle
  (N-first, packed `[E, N, K // 8]`, scales `[E, N, groups]`), runs them
  through `_process_weights_rdna3` and a full MoE forward (w1, SiLU, w2,
  top-k reduce), and compares with a dequantized PyTorch reference. The
  existing tests build the kernel's K-first layout directly and call the op,
  so they never exercised weight processing, which is why this regression
  went unnoticed.
- [x] End to end on 4x RX 7900 XTX with a symmetric compressed-tensors
  checkpoint (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GPTQ W4A16, g32, `pack-quantized`): fails on
  `main` without this change, starts and passes GSM8K with it (below).

## Test results

On gfx1100, in an image built from `main` (df417f780a):

- Without this change, the new test fails for fp16 and bf16: the kernel
  rejects the weights (`group size (K/groups = 1) must be a multiple of 32`),
  because it reads N-first data as K-first.
- With this change (its `int_wna16.py` applied on the same `main` and mounted
  into that image; the C++ kernel is unchanged): the new test passes, and `test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py` passes
  in full (99 passed).
- pre-commit passes, except `update-dockerfile-graph`, which needs
  `/bin/bash` and could not run on my machine.

End to end, on an image built from `main` (df417f780a) for gfx1100, 4x RX
7900 XTX, TP4, `--dtype float16`, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GPTQ W4A16 g32 (symmetric,
compressed-tensors):

- Without this change the engine fails at the first forward:
  `assert self.w1_zp is not None and self.w2_zp is not None`.
- With this change it selects `Rdna3WNA16Experts`, starts, and scores 97.5% on
  GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --num-questions 200
  --temperature 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 2048`, 5-shot, 0% invalid).

The two files of this change were mounted over that image; the C++ kernel is
unchanged. The stock RCCL in the image could not set up P2P between these
GPUs, so it was rebuilt; this is unrelated to this PR.

## AI assistance

I used AI assistance to find the cause and write this change. I have
reviewed every changed line and will run the tests above before marking it
ready.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Store only the current rank's shards in latent MoE up-proj
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On the ROCm path, the routed up-projection in Kimi-K3's latent MoE is built as a `ReplicatedLinear` where each rank holds the full weight. However, the fused tail's `ROCmLatentMoERunner` doesn't need the full weight. Instead, each rank consumes its own shard of up-projection weights, in a column parallel manner, and then a later all-reduce puts the slices back together.

At TP=8, this means that 7/8 of the weights, despite resident on the HBM, is never touched in the fused latent tail path. Across Kimi-K3's 92 MoE layers, this constitute to ~3.9GB per rank of HBM consumed by unused weights, and takes spaces away from useful pools like KV cache.

This PR addresses this by storing only the shard that each rank needs for the latent MoE up-projection, using `ColumnParallelLinear` instead. The computation stays the same as the old fused latent path was already doing the same weight-shard extraction in the live path, and ColumnParallelLinear's weight loader loads only the per-rank shard that it computes on.

In agentic workloads, the saved space from model weights increases the prefix cache pool and hit rate, and improves throughput by ~0.9-30% across concurrencies when KV cache constitutes a binding constraint.

commits.pr_title: [Feat] Structured decisions endpoint (`/v1/systemone`)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR was prepared with the help of AI, but reviewed by myself. This PR description is fully human-written with the exception of the `curl` command below and the test result one-liner.

The current structured decisions server lives as an example. This example is untuned, requires additional setup and could run more effectively inside of vLLM itself.

This implements a new endpoint, with a single question type (`choice`), for AR models only: `POST /v1/systemone`

Example:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
  "state": {"team": "billing", "language": "French"},
  "questions": {
    "team": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Which team does the message name?",
      "criteria": {"billing": null, "shipping": null, "security": null}
    },
    "lang": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Which language does the message name?",
      "criteria": {"English": null, "French": null}
    }
  },
  "seed": 7,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}
}'
```

```json
{
  "id": "decision-80bd0a693f255e1e",
  "object": "structured_decision",
  "created": 1790714266,
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
  "answers": {
    "team": {
      "type": "choice",
      "choice": "billing",
      "probabilities": {"billing": 0.955, "shipping": 0.008, "security": 0.037},
      "confidence": 0.955
    },
    "lang": {
      "type": "choice",
      "choice": "French",
      "probabilities": {"English": 0.0006, "French": 0.9994},
      "confidence": 0.9994
    }
  },
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 254, "output_tokens": 2},
  "diagnostics": {
    "team": {"label_mass": 0.998, "argmax_is_label": true},
    "lang": {"label_mass": 0.9999, "argmax_is_label": true}
  }
}
```


Limits: 64 questions (only `choice`), and options capped at the smaller of the tokenizer's supported label set (see below) and 128.

For a generic endpoint, we need to consider a few things:

### Tokenization

Each model tokenizes differently, so we must ensure that all choice-type questions provide the model a choice between N single-token options in a way that supports the answer format. The server tries labels A to ZZ in the template's answer format and keeps the largest group

### Templates

Decision templates are fixed - we may decide to offer a template in the future if someone needs it.

### Strategies

Decision strategies vary by model: `next_token` covers AR, an upcoming diffusion strategy will cover diffusion and other decision-specific models may wish to ship their own. The model uses `decision_read_strategy` to map the strategy.

Models without a registered read strategy return 501.

---

What's upcoming in future patches in the series:

 - Diffusion will be handled in an upcoming patch
 - Other question types, including those shipped by other providers were not included to keep this patch smaller
 - Probabilities are currently uncalibrated, and it is currently unplanned how we will make those pluggable (punted to the future)
 
## Test Plan

Tests included, against Qwen, proving the request type works.

`pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions`


## Test Result

28 passed on a GB10 (DGX Spark), with this branch's files mounted over a `vllm-openai` nightly image.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Select page-aligned kernel blocks for pooled indexers so the block table addresses storage pages (GLM-5.3-Flash)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58858

GLM-5.3-Flash serving on ROCm silently corrupts its DSA index cache. Root cause: `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returned `[1, MultipleOf(16)]` on ROCm for every deployment, so `select_common_block_size` keeps the hybrid KV manager block (640/1152/2176/4352 for TP8..TP1) as the kernel block size, while `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` drops the spec's `storage_block_size` which every other consumer (cache views, metadata builders, hisparse) already uses as the kernel block. `Glm5NextIndexerCache` with `index_kpool = 4`, however, stores index-cache entries in pool pages of `page * index_kpool` = 128/256 tokens, and both the writer (`get_compressed_slot_mapping`) and the gather address the block table as `column = pos // storage_block_size`. A manager-granular table therefore skips the builder's conversion branch (`storage % kernel != 0`), indexes far outside the request's row (TP2 @32K: raw table 16 columns wide, 256 needed -> page 0 aliased everywhere), and at TP4 writes past the row buffer entirely.

This is also the root cause behind these issues, #55280, #54359 and #56380.

## Changes

* `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py` - `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` is the point where the cache group's spec (`kv_cache_group.kv_cache_spec`) and the group's backends are both in hand, but `storage_block_size` was dropped before dispatch. It now takes `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size` as the kernel block size if the group's backends support it, otherwise falls back to `select_common_block_size` unchanged. On CUDA the indexer declares an exact `[64]`, so the storage block fails validation there and the conversion path keeps working the same way as today. The support check is the existing `block_size_is_supported` logic moved out of `select_common_block_size` to module level, so both call sites use the same check (exact `==` for `int`, multiple-of for `MultipleOf`).

## Test Plan

Sample command gsm8k + bench:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size {2,4} --max-model-len 262144 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser glm47

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template

vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --host localhost --port 8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency 32
```

> If NIAH config is required, I can add in. 

New tests:

* `tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_indexer_block_sizes.py`: `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` returns the storage block (128/256), not the manager block (640/1152/2176/4352), for the kpool group at every TP floor with the real group backends (indexer + tail + aiter sparse MLA) - fails on main as `[640] == [128]`; plus the fallback, backend rejects the storage block (CUDA-style exact `[64]`) or spec without `storage_block_size` -> `select_common_block_size` as before.


## Test Result

| suite |  main (`713ec07`) | this fix |
|---|---|---|
| NIAH 4096-32000, TP2 | 12/28 | **28/28** |
| NIAH 4096-32000, TP4 | 12/28 | **28/28** |
| NIAH 131072/261632, 3 seeds, TP2 | 3/42 | **32/42** | 
| lm-eval gsm8k 20-shot (1319) | 0.8552 ± 0.0097 | **0.9742 ± 0.0044** |

> Likely something else in play for the not 100% NIAH result on long context 131072/261632 case. Fixing that would be out-of-scope of this PR. 

Benchmark (`random` 1024/1024/100, c32, 4 runs incl. `--no-enable-prefix-caching`):

| branch | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `713ec07` | 1017.8 / 1066.7 | 2035.5 / 2133.4 | 24.58 / 24.71 ms | 
| this PR | 1051.4 / 1033.3 | 2102.8 / 2066.5 | 24.90 / 24.97 ms |

In general no difference between main and this PR. 

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_indexer_block_sizes.py  -> 5 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
       tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py          -> 120 passed
test_gpu_model_runner block-size cohort            -> 12 passed
```

P.S. TP8 is not tested, because on the tested main `713ec07` TP8 will produce gibberish outputs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Prevent remote KV reload after decoder preemption
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose MoRIIO WRITE mode performs a one-shot KV transfer from the prefill worker to the decode worker. Under decoder KV-cache pressure, vLLM may preempt and reschedule a request. After the initial transfer, do_remote_prefill is set to False. However, get_num_new_matched_tokens() ignored this flag and incorrectly requested another asynchronous remote-KV load. The second transfer never occurs because the original transfer was already consumed. commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Register HiSparse host pool under single TP Rank
commits.pr_body:
When HiSparse uses its **shared host pool**, all local TP ranks share one `/dev/shm` mmap per DP rank. Even so, every TP rank registers the whole pool with NIXL, and every TP rank READs the same host-pool KV into the same pages. With UCX this means `ibv_reg_mr` of the full pool on every NIC, twice per NIC when relaxed ordering is on. At TP8 with 8 NICs, the pool is registered **128 times per node**, and each request's host-pool KV is pulled **8 times** into identical memory.

This PR adds an opt-in flag, `VLLM_NIXL_HISPARSE_DRAM_RANK0_ONLY=1`, which makes TP rank 0 the only rank that registers the shared pool and pulls into it. The other ranks:

- keep the DRAM regions in their metadata, so the prefill handshake still sees identical region lists;
- skip the DRAM `register_memory`;
- skip the DRAM transfer dlist;
- skip the DRAM part of each READ.

The GPU-resident part (the indexer cache) is still read by every rank, and every rank still notifies the producer.

Completion and ordering need nothing new:

- A request finishes only when all TP ranks report it done.
- HiSparse restores from the shared pool on the next step.
- The `cudaHostRegister` pin of the pool on every rank is unchanged, because each rank's GPU still reads from it.

### Changes

- `vllm/envs.py`: adds `VLLM_NIXL_HISPARSE_DRAM_RANK0_ONLY` (default off).
- `nixl/base_worker.py`:
  - `_leaves_dram_xfer_to_rank0()` decides whether a rank skips. That requires the flag, mixed DRAM/VRAM regions, `tp_rank != 0`, and `use_shared_hisparse_host_pool()`. Private (non-shared) pools are never affected.
  - Skipping ranks:
    - do not register DRAM ranges;
    - store `None` instead of preparing DRAM dlists, in both the local path and the split path;
    - leave zeroing of clipped shared-pool pages to rank 0.
  - Shutdown ignores the `None` handles.
- `nixl/pull_worker.py`: `_read_blocks_mixed()` drops the DRAM descriptors on skipping ranks and keeps the device part. It registers the request even when nothing is left to read, so it still completes and notifies.
- `NixlPushConnector` already rejects mixed-memory KV caches, so it is unchanged.
- Tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py`):
  - **The rank decision:** flag on/off × rank 0 vs non-zero × shared vs private pool.
  - **No DRAM dlist on skipping ranks:** descriptor positions still cover the DRAM regions, so ids stay aligned with the remote side.
  - **A READ that keeps only the device part** still notifies.
  - **A READ left with no descriptors** still completes and notifies.
  - Existing `object.__new__` fixtures initialise the new attribute.

### Why: VM freezes on cloud RoCE VFs

On Cloud VPC instances (QEMU/KVM guests with ConnectX-7 SR-IOV VFs over RoCE, UCX 1.21 via NIXL 1.3.2), a GLM-5.3 HiSparse decode froze **both VMs** during NIXL registration with a 384 GiB pool. There was no guest panic, no guest log and no watchdog output; the nodes had to be reprovisioned. The same configuration passes on bare-metal H200 with InfiniBand.

Guest-side sampling explains the scale of the problem:

- **Pins per page:** `nr_foll_pin_acquired − released` measured exactly **8 + ranks × NICs × 2** (relaxed ordering) per page of pool.
- **Registration metadata:** the VFs' `fw_pages_total` stayed flat at 4 per VF throughout, so the registration metadata is not taken from guest memory.
- **Freeze point:** the freeze appeared between 36.9 TiB (passed) and 49.2 TiB (froze) of NIC-registered memory per VM.

### Results (llmd-roce cluster, GLM-5.3, DeepEP LL decode, 8 NICs, relaxed ordering on unless noted)

**Registration footprint per VM**, from a 2-node decode (DP2 × TP8). These numbers are measured with a startup patch equivalent to this PR on vLLM `87ecf7dbb`.

| Host pool | Stock: pins/page | Stock: NIC-registered | This PR: pins/page | This PR: NIC-registered | This PR: rank-0 registration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 GiB | 136.1x | 12.5 TiB | **24.2x** | **1.58 TiB** | ~28 s (ranks 1–7 < 1 s) |
| 288 GiB | 136x | 36.9 TiB | **24.05x** | **4.51 TiB** | ~80 s |
| 384 GiB | 136x | 49.2 TiB, **both VMs froze** | **24.04x** | **6.01 TiB, passes** | 43–52 s |
| 384 GiB, relaxed ordering off | — | — | 16.02x | 3.01 TiB, passes | 21 s |

Startup is not faster per node: rank 0 does the same per-rank work as before. What drops 8x is the number of registrations, the pinned memory and the NIC metadata.

**P/D correctness**, using a separate prefill and greedy decoding:

- **Results:** P/D output matched the prefill-only reference for 18-, 28.7k- and 250k-token prompts, at pool sizes 100, 288 and 384 GiB. The short prompt shows the usual small numerical divergence between prefill and decode kernels; the 28.7k answer is identical; the 250k answer is the same sentence, differing in one word ("at" vs "in").
- **Transfer count:** each request takes **9** NIXL transfers (rank 0 host + 8 device) instead of 16.
- **Failures:** 0 failed transfers.

**End-to-end benchmark**, 4P/4D, 64 H100:

- **Prefill:** DP4 × PCP8/DCP8.
- **Decode:** DP4 × TP8 with a 288 GiB shared pool.
- **Load:** cc_traces 256k, constant load, 900 s per level.
- **Fairness:** both arms ran on the same 8 nodes, and both roles were re-created between arms.

| Concurrency | Out tok/s (PR vs stock) | TTFT p99 | ITL p50 | ITL p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | **602 vs 503 (+19.7%)** | **21.6 vs 89.0 s** | 20.9 vs 23.3 ms | 116 vs 167 ms |
| 64 | 547 vs 563 | 98.2 vs 87.5 s | 19.2 vs 21.6 ms | 33.3 vs 46.6 ms |
| 128 | 482 vs 520 | 194 vs 183 s | 18.2 vs 20.7 ms | 36.5 vs 65.6 ms |

- **ITL improves at every level:** p50 by 10–12%, p99 by 28–44%.
- **At c64 and c128 both arms are prefill-bound:** request rate is equal within 2%, and the tok/s gap follows output length.

**Transfer totals over the sweep:**

| Metric | This PR | Stock |
|---|---|---|
| NIXL bytes pulled | 5.35 TB | 31.3 TB |
| Average transfer time | 30.8 ms | 122 ms |
| p90 transfer time | 63.7 ms | 318 ms |
| CPU time posting transfers | 472 s | 3,657 s |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Drop the unaccounted, write-only prefill mirror staging buffer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`initialize_hisparse_runtime_buffers` allocates a per-layer prefill mirror staging buffer (`num_layers × max_num_batched_tokens × row_bytes`) after the KV cache is sized, so memory profiling never counts it. That's about 0.69 GiB per GPU for GLM-5.3 (78 layers).

Nothing reads it: `HiSparseConnectorWorker.start_step` sets `mirror_from_resident = True` every step, so the host mirror always copies from the resident cache, and only dummy batches ever wrote the buffer. This PR removes it, along with `mirror_write_target` and `mirror_from_resident`.

Related: #60420.

## Test Plan / Result

1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 8 layers with dummy weights, MNBT 16384, HiSparse with `host_pool_gib=24`. Measured persistent torch memory after init, excluding weights and KV:

| | allocated beyond weights + KV | KV budget |
|---|---|---|
| no HiSparse | 0.7031 GiB | 112.99 GiB |
| HiSparse, main | 0.7756 GiB | 112.96 GiB |
| HiSparse, this PR | 0.7052 GiB | 112.96 GiB |

- Greedy outputs are identical on main and this PR (4 prompts, 300–7000 tokens).
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k "hisparse or profiling"`: 10 passed. The CUDA-only kv-update test now asserts only the resident write.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reject negative --device-ids indices instead of selecting the wrong device
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`EngineArgs._resolve_device_ids` composes `--device-ids` with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`: when CVD is set, each `--device-ids` value is treated as an index into the visible set. The range check only guarded the upper bound:

```python
for i in int_ids:
    if i >= len(cvd_ids):
        raise ValueError(f"--device-ids index {i} is out of range ...")
return [cvd_ids[i] for i in int_ids]
```

A negative index (for example `--device-ids -1`) makes `i >= len(cvd_ids)` evaluate to `False`, so no error is raised and `cvd_ids[i]` silently negative-indexes into the list, resolving to a valid-but-wrong physical device. With `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5` and `--device-ids -1`, the method returns physical device `[5]` instead of rejecting the input.

This completes the bounds check to `not 0 <= i < len(cvd_ids)` so an out-of-range negative index raises the same "out of range" `ValueError` as a too-large one, matching the intent of the existing `test_device_ids_with_cvd_out_of_range` test.

This changes only input validation (silent mis-selection becomes a clear error); it does not affect model output, accuracy, or serving numerics, so no model-evaluation results apply.

**Not a duplicate:** the only open PRs touching this area, #46132 and #41776, add MIG/UUID parsing for `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; neither changes the `_resolve_device_ids` index bounds check. No open issue tracks this.

## Test Plan

Added `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::TestDeviceIds::test_device_ids_with_cvd_negative_index`, mirroring the existing `test_device_ids_with_cvd_out_of_range`:

```bash
pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::TestDeviceIds -q
```

## Test Result

`_resolve_device_ids` does not load a model, so I validated the exact logic on CPU by executing the method against a stubbed platform (a full CUDA build was not available on my machine); the added test runs in CI:

- Before: `EngineArgs(model="m", device_ids=[-1])` with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5` returned `[5]` (no error raised).
- After: it raises `ValueError: --device-ids index -1 is out of range for CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5 (2 devices visible)`.
- Unchanged for valid input: `device_ids=[0, 1]` still resolves to `[4, 5]`.

---

**AI assistance disclosure:** AI assistance was used to help identify and prepare this change, per the repository's contribution policy. The fix is a single bounds-check completion plus a regression test, and I have reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Fuse AttnRes output with per-token FP8 input quantization
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Eligible Kimi-K3 AMD AttnRes outputs currently materialize BF16 activations that the next linear immediately quantizes. Fuse that per-token FP8 conversion into AttnRes and pass native `QuantizedActivation` to supported consumers.

```diff
 AttnRes + output RMSNorm
-  store BF16 → per-token FP8 quant → input GEMM
+  store FP8 + scale → input GEMM
```

Enable the path only for `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and only when all consumers accept the same key. Mixed MoE/router consumers, unsupported linear kernels, and batch-invariant mode retain the original path. Preserve BF16 rounding before quantization and the prefix/block write contract.

This is independent of PD connector work and targets main. Duplicate checks covered #50682, #52968, and #53154: #52968's current diff covers convolution and sigmoid/multiply; #53154 covers MXFP4 output fusions. This PR supplies AttnRes per-token FP8 inputs. The current rowwise Torch FP8 KDA kernel does not expose the required input capability, so this PR does not claim all KDA inputs are fused.

## Evidence

### CI follow-up (2026-10-08)

[Buildkite #93497](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93497) exposed an implicit compiled reference in the FP8 output test when AITER is disabled. Commit `42f0ad593` sets `compile_native=False` for the `QuantFP8` reference, keeping its rounding independent of Inductor fusion. Production code and every numerical tolerance are unchanged. The AttnRes and MLA/KDA direct-return suites pass with AITER disabled (**23 passed**) and enabled (**23 passed**); changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy pass. [Buildkite #93546](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93546) retries the failed K3 step on that commit.


- **Before:** AttnRes and per-token quantization launch separately.
  **After:** A single producer emits activation and scale. Existing + new AttnRes cases passed on all eight MI355X GPUs (16 tests/rank in the final run, including the three capability cases), with exact prefix/block writes, scale rtol 1e-6, and rounding differences limited to an adjacent FP8 code in <1e-4 of values. Three direct-return tests also passed.
- In the paired rank-0 prefill trace, the corresponding standalone AITER per-token quant kernel count falls from 4009 to 3078 (931 calls removed), while AttnRes executes the same 3553 calls.
- `pre-commit run` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`: passed.
- Eight-rank `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_amd_fp8_fusions.py` compares AttnRes + quant + one MLA input GEMM (N2112/K7168), using nine rotated CUDA-graph samples per rank. Median of per-rank medians, four residual blocks:

| Tokens | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 17.110 | 16.597 |
| 256 | 31.701 | 30.168 |
| 4096 | 183.573 | 173.933 |
| 16384 | 682.589 | 657.554 |

This is a producer/projection segment benchmark. One-token results are essentially unchanged; it does not establish a PD throughput gain.

Paired full-model integration validation used the same eight MI355X GPUs, TP8/DCP8, DSpark3 with natural/standard rejection, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, 80 sequences / 16384 batched tokens / 1048576 context. The candidate adds both this PR and the companion DCP prefill fusion #59070 to an exact saved diagnostic baseline; the following model results are combined, not isolated attribution to this PR.

- Three unprofiled repetitions of the same eight-case prefix chain: all 24 first-token outputs, cache-hit counts and computed-token counts match. Median TTFT: cold 32K 1701.03 → 1673.86 ms; exact 32K repeat 83.37 → 77.13 ms; the two other repeats 69.97 → 64.42 and 70.79 → 64.56 ms. The 1024-token append is essentially unchanged (290.44 → 291.09 ms).
- Natural-acceptance C16 decode diagnostic: TPOT 9.867 → 9.840 ms. This is a local single-instance test, not the formal synthetic-AL3 PD C16 benchmark.
- GSM8K, first 128 test examples, 5-shot, seed `0,1234,1234,1234`, concurrency 16, greedy generation, max 8192 output tokens: **127/128 (99.21875%) before and after**, for both extractors. The missed example changes (baseline doc 125; candidate doc 84). Aggregate accuracy is unchanged, but this does not establish per-example equivalence or a full-dataset accuracy result.
- Eight 33K+ context checks (cold and cached): every final arithmetic question is answered correctly. Full continuations match in 7/8 cases; the remaining continuation differs after the correct answer. Outputs/logprobs are not bit-exact.

Evaluation command:

```bash
python -m lm_eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'model=Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:2584/v1/completions,tokenizer_backend=None,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=16,max_retries=1,timeout=1800,max_length=1048576,max_gen_toks=8192' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --limit 128 \
  --gen_kwargs 'max_gen_toks=8192,temperature=0.0,do_sample=False' \
  --seed 0,1234,1234,1234 --log_samples --output_path results
```

Full-dataset accuracy and isolated per-PR model measurements remain review work before merging.


Kernel test/benchmark commands (GPU tests were assigned one pytest process per rank across all eight devices):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py -q
python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node=8 \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_amd_fp8_fusions.py --output results
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

No checkpoint or cache format change. Reverting restores the original computation path.

**Blast Radius:** ROCm

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, analysis, and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Make disable_any_whitespace actually disable whitespace on xgrammar
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`disable_any_whitespace` does not disable whitespace on the xgrammar backend — it **makes whitespace mandatory**, and as a side effect masks out the token the model wants at every JSON value position.

xgrammar's `any_whitespace=False` selects a *fixed* JSON format rather than a whitespace-free one. Its docstring is explicit that the format follows `json.dumps()` conventions, and with `separators` left unset the default is `(", ", ": ")` — *with* spaces. `backend_xgrammar.py` never passes `separators`, so today the flag requires a space after every comma and colon.

The second-order effect is the damaging one. Because the space is mandatory, the bare `"` that opens a string value becomes illegal at the value position. Measured on the mask with a real GLM-5.3 tokenizer, immediately after `{"location":`:

| grammar config | allowed tokens | whitespace-leading | bare `"` | digit-leading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `any_whitespace=True` | 1450 | 719 | yes | 395 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, default separators — **today** | 268 | **268, all of them** | **banned** | 0 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, `separators=(",", ":")` — **this PR** | 703 | **0** | yes | 395 |

The middle row is what vLLM produces now: every legal continuation begins with a space. A model prompted for minified JSON wants the bare `"`; with it masked out, probability mass shifts to the whitespace-prefixed set, where `␣0`, `␣1`, `␣-` compete with `␣"`.

On a production GLM-5.3 deployment this corrupted **26.5%** of `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` responses, returning a number where the first string value belonged:

```
{"location": 2,      "conditions": "cloudy", ...}
{"location": 0.2373, "temperature": 12, ...}
{"location": 0,      "temperature": 0, ... "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

Nothing errors — `finish_reason` and `usage` are normal, so the caller simply receives wrong types.

It is worth noting `json_schema` requests with typed properties were unaffected: a strict schema leaves only `"` legal at that position, so even a forced space yields `␣"` and no digit is reachable. Only permissive grammars (`json_object`, or schemas with loose value types) expose it.

## Fix

Pass compact separators when the flag is set, so it means what its name says:

```python
separators = (",", ":") if self.disable_any_whitespace else None
```

This is strictly better than both current behaviours — genuinely whitespace-free output (0 whitespace-leading tokens) *and* the model's preferred token stays legal.

## Test Plan

Adds `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_whitespace.py`, which inspects the bitmask at the value position after `{"a":`:

- a bare digit and a bare `"` must be legal when whitespace is disabled
- `' 1'` must **not** be legal when whitespace is disabled
- both forms stay legal when whitespace is enabled (guards the default path)

## Test Result

Run against vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b` with xgrammar 0.2.6:

**Before this change — 3 failed, 1 passed.** Each failure is the real defect:

```
FAILED test_compact_value_tokens_survive_disable_any_whitespace[1]   <- bare digit masked
FAILED test_compact_value_tokens_survive_disable_any_whitespace["]   <- bare quote masked
FAILED test_disable_any_whitespace_forbids_the_space                 <- ' 1' legal, i.e. the space was required
1 passed                                                             <- whitespace-enabled control
```

**After this change — 4 passed.**

End-to-end on the affected deployment, n=200 per arm, interleaved, Wilson 95% intervals: `json_object` defect rate **24.0% [16.7, 33.2] → 0.0% [0.0, 1.9]**, whitespace **17.8 → 0.1 chars/response**. The fix is also *cheaper*, since the model minifies on its own once the grammar stops forcing spaces.

## Notes

- `separators` has been part of `compile_json_schema` since well before the pinned xgrammar 0.2.7 (verified present in 0.2.6), and it is ignored when `any_whitespace=True`, so the default path is unchanged.
- The `guidance` backend is unaffected — it maps the same flag to `whitespace_flexible` and was measured clean (0/200) on the same deployment.
- Branch is based on `869f7873` rather than current `main`; the touched region of `backend_xgrammar.py` is byte-identical between the two, and I am happy to rebase.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Always include token_ids in completion stream choices
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Ensure the Rust `/v1/completions` stream includes `token_ids` on every choice when `return_token_ids=true`.

## Claims

- Prompt chunks serialize `token_ids: []` alongside `prompt_token_ids`.
- Generated-token chunks preserve their actual token IDs.
- Terminal chunks serialize `token_ids: []`.
- Requests with `return_token_ids=false` are unchanged.

## Validation

- Manually verified the affected streaming behavior with `return_token_ids=true`.
- Added `completion_stream_serializes_requested_token_ids_on_every_choice`, which serializes the prompt, generated-token, and terminal chunks and asserts their exact `token_ids` values.
- The regression test is covered by the existing Rust Frontend Cargo CI for changes under `rust/`.
- Focused pre-commit checks passed:

  ```bash
  pre-commit run --files rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/completions.rs
  ```

- Rust formatting passed locally in a Rust 1.95 container:

  ```bash
  cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
  ```

- The targeted regression test passed locally in a Rust 1.95 container:

  ```bash
  cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-server \
    completion_stream_serializes_requested_token_ids_on_every_choice
  ```

## Details

`CompletionStreamChoice` skips fields whose value is `None`. Generated deltas already populated `token_ids`, but prompt and terminal choices left the field as `None`, so it disappeared from serialized responses even when requested.

The Python frontend already enforces this contract in [`OpenAIServingCompletion.completion_stream_generator`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bb87d227d4b964abb2a966cdf9194f3d376d9bbe/vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py#L399-L417): every emitted `CompletionResponseStreamChoice` sets `token_ids` to `as_list(output.token_ids)` whenever `return_token_ids` is enabled. This explicitly supplies a list, including an empty list, instead of leaving the optional field unset. The Rust frontend only set the field on generated-token chunks, so prompt and terminal choices omitted it.

The existing stream-yield path now fills only missing `token_ids` values with an empty list when `return_token_ids` is enabled. Centralizing this at emission covers every completion choice while preserving real IDs already attached to generated-token chunks. The only payload change is an empty list on opt-in prompt and terminal chunks; no dependencies or public request fields change.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Preserve small FP8 softmax weights in Triton attention
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Why

The Triton unified-attention kernel casts softmax probabilities to `V.dtype` before `P @ V`. With an FP8 KV cache, small probabilities can underflow to zero and lose meaningful contributions to the attention output.

## Summary

- Scale `P` before its FP8 cast and undo the scale after the FP32 dot. The scale is 256 for NVIDIA E4M3 and 128 for other FP8 formats.
- Add a focused regression test for an `exp(-8)` probability that previously became zero. Existing tests and tolerances are unchanged.

This is the same [low-precision scaling technique](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/2e3a6694ba2f0d8e106f28d2a5d3f6050ebf1572/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm100.py#L85-L90) used by FlashAttention's Blackwell kernel. Its 8-bit path sets [`max_offset = 8`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/2e3a6694ba2f0d8e106f28d2a5d3f6050ebf1572/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm100.py#L2189-L2209), equivalent to scaling `P` by 256 before the low-precision dot.

## Reviewer guide

- `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py` contains the scaling fix.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py` only adds the focused underflow regression.

## Test plan

The exact two-file patch was validated on an NVIDIA B200 in a compatible vLLM checkout; the available GPU image does not include the PyTorch 2.13 environment declared by current `main`.

- `test_fp8_softmax_preserves_small_probabilities`: passes. Before the fix it returns `0.0` instead of `0.0102923084`; after the fix its maximum absolute error is `2.2633e-5` with `atol=5e-5` and `rtol=0.01`.
- Pre-commit passes on both changed files.
- WikiText-2 with [`nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor`](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor), `TRITON_ATTN`, FP8 KV cache, eager execution, and `max_length=2048`: PPL improves from `8.025217` to `8.003337` (`-0.273%`). Of 167 chunks, 123 improve and 44 regress.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Core] Reduce free KV cache queue overhead
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reduce Python overhead in `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue` by reading block links and queue sentinels once into local variables, reusing them for validation and link updates, and handling `popleft_n(1)` inline. The intrusive doubly linked list, eviction order, detached-block link clearing, and existing error checks are preserved.

## Claims

- Singleton allocation/free cycles take about 20% less time on GB300's Grace CPU and 17% less time on Xeon Platinum 8562Y+, with CPython 3.12.13.
- Single pop/append and remove/append cycles also improve; larger batches are mostly unchanged.
- These are isolated queue measurements. End-to-end serving performance and model output evaluations have not been measured.

## Validation

The benchmark compares the original and modified class definitions in separate namespaces using the same actual slotted `KVCacheBlock` class. It measures repeated allocation/free cycles, excluding setup. Both hosts use CPython 3.12.13, one pinned CPU, warmup, randomized baseline/candidate order, pools of 2,048 and 100,000 blocks, and 11 fresh processes with 9 samples per case. A separate 9-process run confirms singleton/two-block batches and removal across two alternating shuffled block orders.

For 100,000 blocks, times are nanoseconds per complete cycle. Percentages are time reductions, computed from the median of per-process candidate/baseline ratios; intervals bootstrap those process ratios. Baseline and modified times are independently aggregated medians.

| Cycle | Grace original → modified | Grace time reduction (95% interval) | Xeon original → modified | Xeon time reduction (95% interval) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `popleft_n(1)` + `append_n` | 313 → 252 ns | 20.3% (19.8–20.6%) | 296 → 247 ns | 17.1% (15.7–19.0%) |
| `popleft()` + `append()` | 203 → 172 ns | 15.3% (14.8–15.5%) | 218 → 192 ns | 11.7% (10.9–12.7%) |
| Hot-block `remove()` + `append()` | 177 → 159 ns | 10.4% (10.1–10.7%) | 181 → 169 ns | 6.4% (5.7–6.7%) |
| Alternating shuffled removal/append, confirmation run | 343 → 319 ns | 4.8% (2.3–6.8%) | 246 → 226 ns | 8.7% (6.9–9.2%) |
| `popleft_n(2)` + `append_n` | 359 → 352 ns | 1.9% (1.1–2.4%) | 346 → 361 ns | **−4.6% (−5.3 to −3.5%)** |
| `popleft_n(8)` + `append_n` | 642 → 634 ns | 1.4% (0.4–2.2%) | 716 → 719 ns | −0.5% (−5.1 to 1.1%) |
| `popleft_n(32)` + `append_n` | 1,779 → 1,757 ns | 1.2% (0.6–1.4%) | 2,152 → 2,121 ns | 1.6% (1.2–2.8%) |
| `popleft_n(128)` + `append_n` | 6,409 → 6,410 ns | 0.0% (−0.4 to 0.9%) | 7,843 → 7,874 ns | −0.4% (−5.2 to 0.6%) |
| Synthetic mix: 90% singleton batches | 348 → 294 ns | 15.5% (15.0–15.6%) | 331 → 295 ns | 11.0% (9.5–11.6%) |

The confirmation run found 20.1% less time for singleton batches on Grace and 17.6% on Xeon. Two-block batches improved by 1.1% on Grace but regressed by 3.6% on Xeon. The synthetic mix contains 90 one-block, 5 two-block, 4 eight-block, and 1 thirty-two-block allocations in a shuffled order; it is not a serving workload.

Hardware: ARM Neoverse V2 / Grace on a GB300; Intel Xeon Platinum 8562Y+

Correctness and static checks:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual \
  --files vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

On the clean PR branch based on upstream main: **389 passed**; all applicable pre-commit hooks and mypy-3.12 passed. 

The benchmark also validates each implementation against a Python list model for 60,000 randomized operations before timing. It checks ordering, counts, forward/backward links, detached links, prepend/append, and cursor iteration after every operation. Both implementations passed on Grace, Xeon, and local ARM macOS. Nine invalid-operation comparisons also preserved exception types/messages and queue state. The added pytest covers complete draining and refilling for batches of 1, 2, and 16. The existing `tests/v1/core` suites are covered by Buildkite.

Full benchmark harness, raw samples, and reproduction commands: [benchmark code, raw samples, and reproduction commands](https://gist.github.com/NickLucche/8bab20301dd9cd74c645875f21667a58). No third-party dependencies are needed for the isolated benchmark. The queue and block class definitions are unchanged between the measured baseline and the PR base commit.

## Details

Normal allocations use `popleft_n()`, while `remove()` is used when touching a cached block whose reference count is zero. The singleton path avoids `range()` iteration and growing the return list with `append()`. For example, `remove()` reads `block.prev_free_block` and `block.next_free_block` into local variables, then uses those same references for the validity check and to reconnect the neighboring blocks. Previously, those steps repeatedly accessed the attributes on `block`. Similarly, `popleft()` and the append methods reuse local references to the head or tail sentinel. This reduces Python attribute accesses; it does not add a cache or change KV-cache behavior. This small path is inlined because calling `popleft()` adds function-call and validation overhead; it preserves the original bulk method's checks and mutations.

The singleton branch is a workload-dependent tradeoff: two-block batches regress by approximately 3–5% on Xeon, although they improve slightly on Grace. Larger batches show little change. This PR deliberately claims only the measured queue effects; no end-to-end throughput, accuracy, or model-output claim is made.

Duplicate-work checks searched open PRs for `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue`, `popleft_n`, and free-block queue performance. Related #59283 and #55841 change eviction/contiguity policy; #40459 explores a Rust control-plane replacement. None implements this Python-only optimization with the existing queue contract. Issue #40244 concerns restoring allocation order; this PR does not address that behavior and is not linked as its fix.

AI assistance was used (OpenAI Codex) for implementation, testing, benchmarking, and this description. The human submitter reviewed the changes before publication.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Make `suppress_stdout` redirect fd 1 instead of `sys.stdout.fileno()`
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59268
Fixes #59269

`suppress_stdout()` wraps gloo process group creation to hide what C code prints to stdout. It redirects `sys.stdout.fileno()` to /dev/null, but C code writes to fd 1, and the two are only the same when `sys.stdout` is the plain process stdout. When they differ:

- `sys.stdout` has no fd, e.g. inside `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())`: `fileno()` raises `io.UnsupportedOperation` (#59268).
- `sys.stdout` is bound to stderr: stderr is sent to /dev/null instead of stdout, so C error output is lost and stdout isn't suppressed (#59269).
- Jupyter on Linux/macOS: ipykernel redirects fd 1 into a pipe that feeds the notebook, and its `OutStream.fileno()` returns a copy of the original terminal fd. The terminal copy gets silenced and the C output still shows up in the notebook.

This redirects fd 1 directly. The rest of the context manager is unchanged. It doesn't affect model output, so there are no evals.

Not a duplicate: neither issue has comments or assignees, and no open PR mentions either issue number or `suppress_stdout`.

## Test Plan

Two tests added to `tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py`, one per issue:

- `test_suppress_stdout_when_sys_stdout_has_no_fd`
- `test_suppress_stdout_keeps_stderr_when_sys_stdout_is_stderr`

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py -v
```

I also checked the #59269 scenario in a plain process, and ran `os.write(1, ...)` inside `suppress_stdout()` in a real Jupyter kernel (ipykernel via `jupyter_client`).

## Test Result

`tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py`:
- main: 2 failed, 2 passed (`io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno`, and fd 1 output not suppressed)
- this PR: 4 passed

#59269 scenario (`sys.stdout = sys.stderr`, then `os.write(1, ...)` and `os.write(2, ...)` inside `suppress_stdout()`):
- main: the stdout line is printed and the stderr line is lost
- this PR: the stdout line is suppressed and the stderr line is printed

Jupyter kernel:
- main: `sys.stdout.fileno()` is 41, and the fd 1 output shows up in the notebook
- this PR: the fd 1 output is suppressed

`pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including mypy for 3.10 and 3.12.

Tested on WSL2 Ubuntu, Python 3.12, CPU-only torch.

AI assistance: I used Claude Code to help investigate and write this fix. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Mamba] Use well-conditioned prompts for FlashInfer ReplaySSM parity tests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the persistently failing `test_replayssm_flashinfer_decode_matches_baseline[v1-nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4]` in the `(H100) ReplaySSM E2E` job. The failure comes from an ill-conditioned prompt, not ReplaySSM: the FlashInfer parity tests now use a prompt that decodes confidently past the replay window. Test-only change.

## Claims

- The FlashInfer ReplaySSM decode (MRV1 + MRV2) and spec-decode parity tests no longer depend on a near-tie in `"Once upon a time, in a small village,"`.
- The Triton/Nano tests keep the original `PROMPTS`; no non-test code changes.

## Validation

Local, 1x H200 (SM90, same as the CI H100), FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1.

Before (reproduces CI):
```
pytest v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py::test_replayssm_flashinfer_decode_matches_baseline -k v1
FAILED ...[v1-...NVFP4] - AssertionError: Test1:
  Matched tokens: [2156, 1486, 1261, 6552, 8401, 8876, 52206, 2274, 20127, 1317, 3346, 1046]
  baseline: ' there was a young girl named Maya who loved to read. a young girl ...'  {' a': -0.68, ...}
  replayssm_flashinfer: ' there was a young girl named Maya who loved to read. apart from ...'  {' apart': -3.51, ...}
```

After:
| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_replayssm_flashinfer_decode_matches_baseline[v1-...]` | passed |
| `test_replayssm_flashinfer_decode_matches_baseline[v2-...]` | passed |
| `test_replayssm_flashinfer_spec_decode_matches_baseline` | passed |

Prompt stability across 5 separately started engines (3 baseline, 2 ReplaySSM; same config as `_check_replayssm_parity`, CUDA graphs on), compared pairwise (10 pairs) with the `check_logprobs_close` rule:

| Prompt | Pairs failing | Min top-1/top-2 margin |
|---|---|---|
| `"Once upon a time, in a small village,"` (old) | 2/10, **including ReplaySSM vs ReplaySSM** | 0.0 (token 1) |
| `"The capital of France is"` | 0/10 | 0.0–0.5 |
| `"It was the best of times, it was the worst of times,"` (new) | 0/10, exact match in all 10 | ≥ 1.25 |

## Details

**Root cause.** The NVFP4 Nemotron-3.5 checkpoint does not produce bitwise-identical logits across engine instances, even with an identical baseline config: three baseline-only engines disagreed on prompt 1 from the first generated token (`" there was"` vs `" there lived"`, margin 0–0.12). The `" there was"` branch falls into a degenerate repetition (`"...loved to read. a young girl named Maya..."`) with a nearly flat next-token distribution, where run-to-run noise pushes one side's token out of the other side's top-5. Two identically configured ReplaySSM engines fail `check_logprobs_close` against each other the same way, and baseline-vs-ReplaySSM divergence is within baseline-vs-baseline divergence, so ReplaySSM numerics are not the cause. I also checked that vLLM's ring-tracker advance matches the FlashInfer `checkpointing_ssu` flush rule (`prev_k + T > MAX_WINDOW`).

**Fix.** Add `FLASHINFER_PROMPTS`, replacing the fragile prompt with `"It was the best of times, it was the worst of times,"`, which decodes all 32 tokens confidently and so still exercises the 16-token window flush/replay. The spec-decode parity test uses the same model and prompts and is switched too. `test_replayssm_flashinfer_mtp` only checks output length and is unchanged.

**Limitations / follow-up.** The underlying run-to-run non-determinism of the NVFP4 baseline (likely MoE kernel/autotune selection) is not addressed here.

**Duplicate check.** Searched issues/PRs for `test_replayssm_decode`, `replayssm_flashinfer_decode_matches_baseline`, and related keywords: none found. Of the open PRs touching this test file (#46239, #47576, #48792, #49847, #49887, #50380, #52962, #55688), none changes these prompts or addresses this failure. #55688 restructures the file's constants and may need a trivial rebase.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Drain async KV loads in pause(mode="wait"), and pause the drain test only once a request is in flight
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`test_dp_pause_wait_mode_drains_in_flight` fails with `TimeoutError` on both NVIDIA and AMD CI: [build 93523](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93523/list?sid=01a11a1e-c1e8-44d7-9812-92921eb57d06&tab=output).

This also takes over #59993 with the author's agreement, so there are two commits, each standing on its own.

1. The engine fix from #59993, carried over unchanged. Under PAUSED_NEW a request whose async KV connector load was admitted before the pause sits in `kv_holding_waiting` and still holds KV blocks, but `get_num_unfinished_requests()` counted only `running` and `schedule()` admitted from neither waiting queue. The engine looked idle while blocks were still allocated, the following prefix cache reset raised `Failed to reset KV cache even when all the running requests are preempted ...`, the `pause` or `sleep` call failed with HTTP 500, and the scheduler stayed paused.

2. The test fix for the timeout above. The test adds a request and pauses with `mode="wait"` straight away, without waiting for it to start. If the pause wins the race the request is still in `waiting`, where it holds no blocks and is invisible to the drain, so the drain resolves at once and the request stays queued until resume. The test then waits 30 s for output that cannot arrive while paused.

## Cause

Both come down to what counts as in flight for a `mode="wait"` drain. In the engine it was too narrow: requests holding KV blocks are in flight in every sense that matters to a cache reset, yet the paused count ignored them. In the test the request was simply not in flight yet.

Nothing is wrong with the engine in the second case. A request that is accepted but not yet scheduled holds nothing, so a pause arriving before it starts is correct to resolve immediately. The test has to let it start first, which is the convention the author already set in `test_dp_pause_late_request_does_not_block_drain` in the same file:

> Run a wave first, so the engines are quiesced by the pause rather than by never having started, and drain has something to observe.

## Fix

`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` and `vllm/v1/core/sched/interface.py` count `kv_holding_waiting` under PAUSED_NEW, minus streaming sessions waiting for input as the unpaused count already does, and let `schedule()` admit only from `kv_holding_waiting` while paused. Requests holding no blocks keep waiting until resume, and PAUSED_ALL is untouched. Two new CPU tests come with it in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`.

`tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py` waits for the first output before calling `pause_generation(mode="wait")`. Three lines, no new helper.

## Validation

The engine bug reproduces on `main` with the new CPU tests, raising exactly the reported error, and passes with the fix:

```
before:  2 failed, 1 passed   (RuntimeError: Failed to reset KV cache ...)
after:   3 passed
```

The test race was made deterministic by delaying the engine side handling of the add so the pause always arrives first. With the engine fix applied but the test unchanged it still fails, which shows the two are independent:

```
before:  1 failed   (TimeoutError)
after:   1 passed in 29.92s
```

The whole pause family passes, one test per process:

```
tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k pause   12 passed
```

commits.pr_title: [CI] Make (H100) Distributed DP + EP optional
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Mark `:nvidia: (H100) Distributed DP + EP` (`distributed-tests-8xh100`) as `optional` so it no longer blocks PR builds. Its AMD MI355 mirror is pinned to `optional: false` so it keeps running as before.

## Claims

- PR builds no longer wait on an 8×H100 node for this step.
- Coverage is unchanged for nightly builds and for the MI355 mirror. The H100 step can still be unblocked manually on any PR.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml` passes, including the step-key and test-tethering hooks.
- I checked the ci-infra pipeline generator (`buildkite/pipeline_generator/buildkite_step.py`):
  - Optional steps are skipped on PRs but still run when `nightly == "1"`.
  - AMD mirrors take `amd.get("optional", step.optional)`, so without the explicit `optional: false` the MI355 mirror would have become optional too.
  - The same override is already used in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`.

## Details

This is the only non-optional step in the `ci` pipeline that needs a whole 8-GPU node. Every other 8-GPU step (H200 LM evals, DSv4-Flash disagg, the AMD 8-GPU evals) is already optional. On `mithril-h100-pool`, smaller jobs keep the GPUs on each node split up, so this step can sit in `reserved` for hours. For example, in https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93472 it was the only unfinished job. It became runnable at 01:24 UTC and still had not started at 04:30 UTC.

Tradeoff: PRs touching `vllm/distributed/`, `vllm/config/parallel.py`, etc. no longer get NVIDIA DP+EP (torchrun tp=2/dp=4 with EP) coverage automatically. That coverage comes from the nightly build, from the MI355 mirror on each PR, or from unblocking the step manually.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this step (searched for `distributed-tests-8xh100` and "Distributed DP + EP optional").
