commits.pr_title: Remove Python 3.10 support now that it is EOL
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python 3.10 reached end of life this month, so the minimum supported version becomes 3.11. Follows the same shape as #26416, which dropped 3.9.

## Claims

- `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.15"`. The 3.10 classifier, the CMake supported version and the cp310 `triton-cpu` wheel are removed.
- `spinloop` and `fs_io_C` no longer need a Python 3.11 guard in `CMakeLists.txt` or `setup.py`.
- Version-gated code is simplified: `USE_SCHED_YIELD` in `vllm/distributed/utils.py`, the `sre_parse`/`sre_constants` fallback in `backend_outlines.py`, and the `co_qualname` TODO in `vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py`.
- `backend_outlines.py` imports `re._parser` and `re._constants` directly instead of going through `importlib`. `check_forbidden_imports.py` allows exactly that import, because `regex` has no equivalent.
- mypy runs once, on the minimum supported version, in a single `mypy` hook. The 3.12 and 3.13 CI-only hooks are removed, ahead of a move to `ty`, which will only check the lowest version.
- Ruff's pyupgrade fixes for a 3.11 target are applied: `typing_extensions` imports of `Self`, `assert_never`, `Never`, `Required`, `NotRequired` and others move to `typing`, and `asyncio.TimeoutError` becomes `TimeoutError`. `TypedDict` stays on `typing_extensions` because pydantic needs it before 3.12.
- `UP042` (`(str, Enum)` to `StrEnum`) is ignored for now, because it changes `str()`/`format()` output for 18 enum classes. That will be audited in a follow-up.
- Docs list Python 3.11 to 3.14, and the SkyPilot examples use `python=3.12`.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files, using the pinned ruff 0.14.0.
- `pre-commit run mypy --all-files`: the same 3 errors as `mypy-3.10` on `main`. They come from Linux-only `os`/`mmap` APIs and only appear when checking on macOS.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py`: 11 passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/structured_output -k outlines`: 22 passed.
- I checked the forbidden-import pattern by hand. `from re import _constants, _parser` passes. `import re`, `from re import compile`, `from re import _parser, compile` and `from re import _parser as p` are still rejected.

commits.pr_title: [Model][GLM-5.3-Flash] Warm up the DCP top-k merge kernels for the kpool indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59211 (now merged; this branch is rebased on main).

Under DCP, the GLM-5.x kpool indexer merges the per-rank top-k with `_merge_dcp_topk_global`, which runs `PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel` and `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`. Only `SparseAttnIndexer.__init__` registers these kernels for JIT warmup, so with the kpool indexer they were compiled on the first long-context request:

```
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:140] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel.kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config.
```

This PR registers them from `SparseAttnIndexerKpool.__init__` under the same conditions: DCP > 1, JIT warmup enabled, CUDA, and CuteDSL available. #59211 already makes the warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.

## Test Plan

`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on 8×H100 with `vllm serve`, bf16 KV cache, no MTP. TP8 + DCP8 with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`, compared with TP8. GSM8K (1319 questions) at 5, 25, 50 and 100 shots, i.e. prompts from about 650 to about 17k tokens. Checked the server log for JIT monitor warnings.

## Test Result

`PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel` no longer compiles during inference under DCP8. Without this change, it compiled during inference in the same setup. The other JIT warnings in the log (`fused_moe_kernel`, kpool compress kernels) also appear without DCP and are unrelated.

| Shots | TP8 | TP8 + DCP8 |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.918 | 0.920 |
| 25 | 0.914 | 0.917 |
| 50 | 0.911 | 0.911 |
| 100 | 0.917 | 0.921 |

The E2E runs used the same local SM90 FlashMLA bf16 DCP change as #59211, which Hopper needs for DCP at head_dim 512.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs for kpool / `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` / `PackDCPTopkCandidates` warmup and found none. #54345 deals with prefill metadata JIT, not the DCP top-k merge kernels.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Enroll five steps in automatic sharding
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

First pilot of automatic sharding (vllm-project/ci-infra#700). This adds `automatic_shard: true` to five steps whose commands are plain pytest:

| Step | Planned shards |
|---|---|
| `entrypoints-integration-api-server-openai-chat_completion` | 2 |
| `entrypoints-integration-pooling` | 2 |
| `kernels-mamba-test` | 3 |
| `quantized-models-test` | 2 |
| `v1-spec-decode` | 2 |

At pipeline generation, the generator packs each step's test files into shards of up to 18 minutes of test time, using main's per-file timings. It then runs the step as one job with `parallelism: N`, and a pytest plugin keeps only that shard's tests. If timings are missing or planning fails, the step runs as its usual single job.

The AMD mirror of `v1-spec-decode` inherits the flag. The generator doesn't shard AMD steps, so the mirror still runs as one job.

## Test Plan

- Ran ci-infra's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against this checkout. All five steps produce a plan within budget, with the shard counts shown above.
- This PR's CI build should show each step as N parallel shard jobs, with a planning annotation. Every collected test should run in exactly one shard.

commits.pr_title: [XPU] Add tuned Mamba SSU configs for 2 more B70 shapes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#50534 tuned Mamba `selective_state_update` configs for Intel Arc Pro B70 across `headdim=64,dstate={16,32,64,128,256}` but shipped only `headdim=64,dstate=128` and `headdim=128,dstate=256`, dropping the other shapes because no on-hand model exercised them. #56765 (Intel Arc Pro B60, open) later shipped exactly two of those dropped shapes — `headdim=64,dstate=64` (`Zyphra/Zamba2-2.7B-instruct`) and `headdim=64,dstate=256` (`tiiuae/Falcon-H1-1.5B-Instruct`) — proving real models exercise them. This PR adds the corresponding B70 files. No code changes.

## Duplicate-work check

Per `AGENTS.md`: searched open PRs for `selective_state_update`/`mamba ssu config`/`B70` — no open PR covers these two shapes for B70. The closest related PR is #48980 (opt-in warmup-time SSU autotune), which is complementary: its lookup order keeps "bundled configuration" as a fallback tier below the autotune cache, so this addition remains useful regardless of whether #48980 lands.

## Changes

4 files under `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/configs/selective_state_update/`:
- `headdim=64,dstate=64` float16 + float32 (Zamba2-2.7B, `ngroups=1`, `nheads=80`)
- `headdim=64,dstate=256` float16 + float32 (Falcon-H1-1.5B, `ngroups=1`, `nheads=48`)

Shapes/ngroups/nheads confirmed against each model's real HF `config.json`, not assumed.

## Method

Generated on 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 (32GB), one card per (shape, cache_dtype) pair, via `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_selective_state_update.py --save-configs --compare --validate`, with `--ngroups 1` matching each model's real config (the script's own default is `ngroups=8`, which #50534 flagged as a mismatch vs. real models). Every shipped entry passed `--validate` against the fp32 reference; entries that failed to validate were dropped, not shipped.

## Results

### headdim=64, dstate=64 (Zamba2-2.7B)

| cache_dtype | kernel speedup | validated | E2E (`vllm bench serve`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| float16 | 1.44x–2.77x | 11/11 | +4–5% TPOT/throughput (cc 1/8/32) |
| float32 | 1.01x–1.72x | 11/11 | flat to +0.8% (cc 8/32) |

### headdim=64, dstate=256 (Falcon-H1-1.5B)

| cache_dtype | kernel speedup | validated | E2E (`vllm bench serve`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| float16 | 3.21x–7.75x | 11/11 | 1.68x TPOT / 1.64x throughput @ cc=64 |
| float32 | 1.96x–5.16x | 9/9 | 1.62x TPOT/throughput @ cc=64 |

## Test plan

- `--validate` every shipped entry against the fp32 reference (see per-shape counts above); failing entries dropped rather than shipped.
- `pre-commit run` on the 4 changed files — all applicable hooks pass (JSON-only diff, no Python/lint-relevant changes).
- `vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`, tuned vs. heuristic (config file present vs. removed), on the real target models, confirmed via server log line showing which config was actually loaded.
- No CUDA/ROCm behavior changes — data-only addition of two new device/shape entries.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Preserve cache_salt for chunked embeddings
[Rust Frontend] Preserve explicit zero sampling values in gRPC requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Preserve explicit `top_k=0` and `min_p=0` across the Rust gRPC API so callers can disable model-provided sampling filters. Make `top_p` optional for consistency and pass explicit values through to the shared validator, matching the HTTP `generate` API.

## Claims

- With model defaults `top_k=8` and `min_p=0.2`, explicit zero reaches engine-core as zero; omitted values inherit the model defaults.
- Omitted `top_p` inherits the model default. Explicit `top_p=0` returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; valid values in `(0, 1]` remain explicit overrides, including `top_p=1` to disable the filter.
- Add presence to the three sampling fields without changing their protobuf field numbers or wire types.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p vllm-server --lib -- --quiet
```

437 tests passed. Scoped pre-commit checks passed for all three changed files.

The existing regression checks protobuf serialization, gRPC conversion, and text lowering for omitted, disabled, and positive sampling values against nonzero model defaults, for both unary and streaming conversion. The existing gRPC invalid-sampling test now covers both `top_p=0` and `top_p=2`. The zero case reproduced the bug before the fix (a successful response) and passes after the fix (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`).

No real-model/GPU validation has been performed.

## Details

Proto3 scalars without presence collapse explicit zero into omission. `optional` lets the converter preserve zero for `top_k` and `min_p` instead of falling back to model defaults. Explicit `top_p=0` is preserved so the shared validator rejects it: valid engine values are in `(0, 1]`. This addresses [Bugen's review comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60115#discussion_r4205210352).

Generated Rust fields become `Option<T>`. Regenerate clients to send explicit zero for `top_k` and `min_p`; clients that omit these fields retain their previous behavior, and older servers retain their previous interpretation. The crate version bump remains separate.

This fixes the existing typed API. Related #56776 proposes a separate native-sampling JSON payload. The additional generation fields and cached usage are in #59837; reasoning controls are in #59836. These PRs target `main` independently.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix fused Gumbel-max wrapping-window bias
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes biased V1 CPU sampling from the fused Gumbel table in #53913. `fused_gumbel_argmax` now draws independent 53-bit Gumbel noise per `(seed, token)` via SplitMix64, which is the #59786 wrapping-window bug.


## Claims

- Fixes #59786: consecutive seeds are no longer a 1-token table shift; large-vocab Zipf head/tail match softmax; previously unreachable IDs are reachable.
- Serving top-k / top-p stays as fast or faster (skip `-inf` with a bounded-Gumbel prune).
- Full-vocab random sampling is slower than the old sequential table, but still faster than stock PyTorch and statistically correct.
- Greedy is unchanged and still matches `torch.argmax`.


## Details
Root cause. g_gumbel_table[(seed + i) & (2^20 - 1)] makes every row one sliding window of a single 1M-entry table. Enumerating windows on Zipf(1.1), V=151936 (from #59786): TV≈0.07 vs softmax, 79078 / 151936 tokens never win, P(top-1) 0.141 vs 0.132. The old chi-squared test used small_vocab=100, so it missed this. GPU / MRV2 Triton Gumbel was already unbiased; V1 CPU is the default on non-x86 (no triton-cpu wheel).

Fix. Drop the table. Each row keys SplitMix64(seed); token i gets 53-bit u and score logit - log(-log u). Consecutive seeds no longer share a shifted window.

Perf tradeoff. Top-k/top-p leave most logits -inf. x + 37.5 <= best_score skips those, so serving batches got faster than the old full-vocab SIMD add. Unfiltered random must visit the live vocab with RNG/exp/log, so fused latency rose (e.g. batch=1 random 0.44 ms → 6.17 ms). That path is uncommon next to top-k/top-p.

Other. OpenMP over rows, no fork at batch=1. greedy_argmax unchanged. RISCV still use forward_native.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Use FusedMoEWithLoRA for shared MoE LoRAs on 3D models
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60093. `--enable-moe-shared-loras` on a 3D-weight MoE model crashed during LoRA warmup because the experts module was still wrapped in `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA`, which never builds `lora_a_stacked`.

## Claims

- Shared-outer MoE adapters (`experts.w1` / `experts.w2` / `experts.w3`) now use `FusedMoEWithLoRA` on 3D-weight models such as GPT-OSS.
- Engine startup with `--enable-lora --enable-moe-shared-loras` completes warmup instead of raising `AttributeError: 'MoERunner' object has no attribute 'lora_a_stacked'`.
- 3D PEFT adapters without this flag still use `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA`.

## Validation

Reproduced the crash and the fix on a Colab Tesla T4 (16 GB, compute capability 7.5, driver 580.82.07), vLLM 0.31.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The checkpoint was `openai/gpt-oss-20b` cut to 1 layer and 8 experts, unquantized, `load_format=dummy`, float16, so the run fits the T4. `LLM()` takes the same profile run as `vllm serve`.

Before the change, model load succeeded (2.62 GiB) and warmup failed in `create_dummy_lora`:

```text
AttributeError: 'MoERunner' object has no attribute 'lora_a_stacked'
```

After the wrapper change, the same `LLM()` call returns. vLLM 0.31.0 with this patch applied to `vllm/lora/model_manager.py` finished warmup (`PY_EXIT:0`) on that T4. The previous run, identical except for the patch, died in `create_dummy_lora`.

A second load of that engine printed:

```text
model GptOssForCausalLM
WRAPPER FusedMoEWithLoRA shared True lora_a_stacked True n 24
```

The full 24-layer mxfp4 `vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b` command was not run. The failure and the fix are both in wrapper selection during warmup, before any token is generated. CI does not currently run an `enable_moe_shared_loras` test; there was no existing coverage to extend without a GPU MoE checkpoint.

## Details

`enable_moe_shared_loras` rewrites the experts packed mapping to `["experts.w1", "experts.w2", "experts.w3"]`. `create_dummy_lora` then treats the module as packed and indexes `lora_a_stacked`. That list is built only by `FusedMoEWithLoRA.create_lora_weights`, which also reads the flag and collapses the shared factors to expert-dim 1. `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA` overrides `create_lora_weights`, ignores the flag, and keeps the fused gate/up pair (`set_lora` requires two tensors).

The manager already forces `FusedMoEWithLoRA` for `--enable-mixed-moe-lora-format`. Shared-outer adapters are the same 2D layout, so a 3D base model has to use that wrapper too. `_is_3d_moe_model` stays true only when neither flag is set, which preserves the fused PEFT path.

Limitation: a 3D PEFT checkpoint (fused gate/up on disk) is not a shared-outer adapter. Serving that file still requires leaving `enable_moe_shared_loras` off, or converting it under `--enable-mixed-moe-lora-format`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quant] Read safetensors headers of checkpoints with other file names
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

A GPTQ checkpoint whose weights are not named `model.safetensors` fails to load whenever they are not already in the local cache, because the lookup that decides which layers are quantized cannot see the file and every linear layer is then built unquantized.

Failure in CI: [build 93298](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93298/list?jid=01a11652-3695-4590-86b6-eda1b6ced9ea&tab=output)

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.qweight'
in LlamaModel. The available parameters belonging to layers.0.mlp.down_proj
(RowParallelLinear) are: {'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight'}
```

## Cause

`modules_in_block_to_quantize` is optional, and older GPTQ checkpoints do not carry it, so `AutoGPTQConfig.maybe_update_config` derives the list from the safetensors headers. That goes through `HfApi.get_safetensors_metadata`, which asks for two fixed names only, `model.safetensors` and its index.

`LnL-AI/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-GPTQ-4bit` stores its weights in `gptq_model-4bit-128g.safetensors`, so the call always raises `NotASafetensorsRepoError`. That error is fatal, so it is raised without a log line and swallowed, which is why nothing shows up in the logs. The only remaining fallback reads the local cache, where files are matched by `*.safetensors` and the odd name is found, so a warm cache is the only reason this ever worked.

AWQ handles the same checkpoint shape correctly because it derives the complement, so an empty answer excludes nothing instead of excluding everything.

Nothing changed in `safetensors` or `huggingface_hub`. The local cache fallback added in #43197 has been masking it since, and this checkpoint only entered the test in #54809, so CI has only ever met it through a warm shared cache.

## Fix

When the fixed-name lookup fails, list the files the repo actually has and read the headers of every `*.safetensors` among them, the way the weight loader already locates weights. Only headers are fetched.

An empty module list now also means "unknown" rather than "nothing is quantized", so a machine with no network at all still loads the checkpoint. This is reachable only for GPTQ checkpoints without the field, and only when no metadata can be read by any route.

## Validation

Cold cache, the test that fails in CI: `1 failed in 21.16s` before, `1 passed in 52.56s` after. With the metadata forced empty, standing in for a machine with no network: `1 failed in 16.30s` before, `1 passed in 48.32s` after. Cold cache, both `test_quantization` parameters plus `quantization/test_auto_gptq.py`: `10 passed in 105.78s`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix ZeroDivisionError in Qwen3-VL video sampling when the source fps is unknown
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Fixes #60212. When the source fps is unknown, vLLM's video decoders report it as 0, and `Qwen3VLVideoBackend` then raised `ZeroDivisionError`. In that case it now assumes 24 fps, which is what HF's `Qwen3VLVideoProcessor` does. ## Claims - Qwen3-VL frame sampling no longer divides by zero when the source fps is unknown. - The assumed 24 fps is also stored in the video metadata, so the frame timestamp step no longer divides by zero either. Frame indices, metadata fps and timestamps match HF. A known fps does not change. - For the input in the issue (DeepStream backend, MP4 with `moov` after `mdat`), the request now ends in the existing `ValueError("DeepStream backend received no frame indices")` (HTTP 400). Before, it ended in an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError`. - Adds `tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_qwen3_vl_unknown_source_fps_matches_hf`. ## Validation Setup: vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a` (commit `92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691`, precompiled editable install), transformers 5.18.0, `nvidia-deepstream-videodecode-cu13==9.0.2`, on 2× NVIDIA L40S (driver 595.58.03, CUDA 13.2). The code that fails is pure Python and does not use the GPU. Reproducer, run as `python -P repro.py`. It gives the sampler the values that `probe_metadata()` returned for an MP4 with a trailing `moov` (see "How the probe values were measured" below): ```python try: from vllm.multimodal.video import Qwen3VLVideoBackend from vllm.multimodal.video_decoders.base import VideoSourceMetadata, VideoTargetMetadata # Values probe_metadata returns for moov_at_end.mp4 source = VideoSourceMetadata(total_frames_num=0, original_fps=0.0, duration=0.0) target = VideoTargetMetadata(num_frames=-1, fps=1, max_duration=300) result = Qwen3VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample( source=source, target=target, ) print(f"No error. indices={result}") except ZeroDivisionError as e: print(f"ZeroDivisionError reproduced: {e!r}") print("REPRODUCED") except Exception as e: print(f"Other error ({type(e).__name__}): {e}") ``` | Tree | Runs | Output | | --- | --- | --- | | `92044241a` (before) | 2: one in the `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image, one in a venv | `ZeroDivisionError reproduced: ZeroDivisionError('float division by zero')` | | this PR | 2: one in the fix session, one in a separate review session | `No error. indices=[]` | `[]` is also what HF's `sample_frames` returns for 0 frames and `fps=None`. The full script used in these runs also had a Part 1 that runs the DeepStream probe on MP4 files. The venv machine had no ffmpeg to make those files, so in the venv runs Part 1 only printed `FileNotFoundError`. The script above is Part 2, which is where the bug is. Other checks on the patched tree: - New test: `python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider tests/multimodal/test_video.py -k "qwen3_vl or cosmos3"` gives `2 passed, 89 deselected`. (`--noconftest` is only there because our venv did not have `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports.) On the base code the test fails with `ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero` (`vllm/multimodal/video.py:380`). With a 24 fps fallback inside the sampler only, it fails with `assert 0.0 == 24` on the metadata fps. - `test_video_processor_from_model_repo[qwen3vl]` passes. It compares vLLM's indices with the real `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` HF processor for 12 fps/duration pairs, so behaviour with a known fps is unchanged. - `tests/multimodal/test_video.py -k "not pynvvideocodec and not torchcodec"`: 51 passed, 1 skipped, 7 failed. All 7 failures come from our setup and happen before any sampling. In 6 `test_video_processor_from_model_repo` cases the HF cache directory was not writable. `test_video_backend_handles_edit_list_trimmed_video` needs `av`, which was not installed. The `qwen3vl` case above passed once `av` was installed and the HF cache was writable. - Path check (the script is not in this PR): DeepStream, with the probe stubbed to `(0, 0.0, 0.0, 0, 0, '')`, ends in `ValueError: DeepStream backend received no frame indices` (HTTP 400). OpenCV with a real 90-frame video and the fps reported as 0 loads with metadata fps `24.0`, and the timestamps are computed. - vLLM side by side with HF (`sample_frames` with `fps=None`, then `_calculate_timestamps`): indices, metadata fps and timestamps match for 1800, 90, 3 and 0 frames with unknown fps, and for 1800 frames at 30 fps. - `pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/video.py tests/multimodal/test_video.py` passes. Not done: there was no `vllm serve` run with a Qwen3-VL model. The real DeepStream probe was not run on the patched tree, because the venv machine had no ffmpeg or `gi`.
How the probe values were measured (before the fix, in the vllm/vllm-openai nightly image at the same commit) Image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:669978fee946df1ef1f0169090e26392b3cf1071cb2386cb93be2141872d35c7`, GStreamer 1.24.2, same GPUs. Inside the image: ```bash apt-get update && apt-get install -y ffmpeg gstreamer1.0-tools gstreamer1.0-plugins-base gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-libav python3-gi python3-gst-1.0 libv4l-0 pip install "nvidia-deepstream-videodecode-cu13==9.0.2" ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=30 -t 60 -c:v libx264 -b:v 4M -pix_fmt yuv420p /tmp/moov_at_end.mp4 ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i /tmp/moov_at_end.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart /tmp/moov_at_start.mp4 ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i /tmp/moov_at_end.mp4 -c copy -movflags frag_keyframe+empty_moov /tmp/fragmented.mp4 ``` ```python from nvidia.deepstream_videodecode import probe_metadata for f in ["/tmp/moov_at_end.mp4", "/tmp/moov_at_start.mp4", "/tmp/fragmented.mp4"]: print(f"{f}: {probe_metadata(open(f, 'rb').read())}") ``` ``` /tmp/moov_at_end.mp4: (0, 0.0, 0.0, 0, 0, '') /tmp/moov_at_start.mp4: (1800, 30.0, 60.0, 1280, 720, 'h264') /tmp/fragmented.mp4: (250, 30.0, 8.333, 1280, 720, 'h264') ``` `cuda-libraries-13-0` was not installed, so the NVDEC GStreamer plugins warned at startup (`libnppig.so.13` missing). The probe only uses `qtdemux`, which loaded.
## Details **Root cause.** When vLLM's decoders do not know the source fps, they report it as `0`. The DeepStream probe returns `(0, 0.0, 0.0, 0, 0, '')` for an MP4 whose `moov` box comes after `mdat`. OpenCV (`CAP_PROP_FPS`) and torchcodec (`average_fps` of `None`) also give 0. `Qwen3VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` is a port of HF's `Qwen3VLVideoProcessor.sample_frames`, but the port left out HF's unknown-fps branch, `if metadata.fps is None: metadata.fps = 24`. So `int(total_frames_num / original_fps * fps)` divides by 0. HF's branch also writes 24 into the metadata. In vLLM, the 0 was passed on into the metadata through `create_hf_metadata`, and `Qwen3VLProcessingInfo._get_video_second_idx` and `_calculate_timestamps` divide by it too. So a fallback in the sampler alone only moves the crash to the timestamp step. **Fix.** `Qwen3VLVideoBackend` now overrides the existing `VideoLoader._prepare_source` hook. `DynamicVideoBackend` and `GLMGAVideoBackend` already override it in the same way. All four decoders (OpenCV, torchcodec, PyNvVideoCodec, DeepStream) call this hook before sampling, and `create_hf_metadata` builds the metadata from its result. If the fps is not positive, the hook returns the source with fps `24.0`. Now the sampler, the metadata and the timestamps all use the same fps. The sampler also calls the hook at the start, so a direct call (like the reproducer) gets the same fps. On the decoder path this second call changes nothing. **Limitations.** - The all-zero probe result comes from the third-party `nvidia-deepstream-videodecode` wheel. So does the short frame count for a fragmented MP4 (250 frames, 8.333 s, for a 60 s clip). This PR does not change either. A trailing-`moov` MP4 on the DeepStream backend still fails, but now with HTTP 400. The message ("DeepStream backend received no frame indices") does not say that the probe could not read the file. A clearer message would be a separate change. - HF logs a warning when it assumes 24 fps. This hook does not log, the same as the other `_prepare_source` overrides in the file. I can add a log line if reviewers want one. - `duration` stays as reported (0). HF does not change it in this branch, and no Qwen3-VL step reads it. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Eliminate frontend ZMQ port TOCTOU with inherited listeners
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Fix the frontend ZMQ port TOCTOU by keeping the kernel listener bound continuously from port allocation through frontend startup.

The supervisor now:

1. binds each TCP or IPC listener before engine or frontend launch;
2. records the resolved endpoint;
3. passes the listener to the Python child or Rust subprocess;
4. closes its own descriptor copy after a successful spawn.

Python frontends adopt the socket with `ZMQ_USE_FD`. The Rust frontend receives the two listener descriptors through its existing CLI bootstrap boundary and moves them into zeromq. Engines and Ray actors receive resolved endpoints before construction.

This removes the frontend-to-supervisor address report protocol and its pipe/stdout coordination.

## Context and relationship to existing work

#42585 identified the probe-release-bind race and fixed the ordinary Python path with child-side binding plus address report-back.

#51033 extends that protocol to Rust and Ray DP. This draft implements the materially different design proposed in [review 5045545604](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51033#pullrequestreview-5045545604): the supervisor owns the initial bind and transfers the already-bound listener to the final frontend owner.

The alternatives have different lifecycle shapes:

```text
#51033:
supervisor creates :0 template
  -> frontend binds
  -> frontend reports resolved address
  -> supervisor mutates startup state
  -> engines receive address

this draft:
supervisor binds raw listener and gets resolved address
  -> engines receive address
  -> frontend inherits listener
  -> parent closes its descriptor copy
```

This draft intentionally overlaps #51033 so reviewers can evaluate the ownership-transfer approach directly. Searches for `42585 in:body`, `inherited ZMQ listener`, and `ZMQ TOCTOU` found #51033 and no other open implementation of listener transfer.

## Ownership model

- `EngineZmqBindAddresses` contains bind templates such as `tcp://host:0`.
- `EngineZmqListeners` owns the supervisor-bound raw sockets.
- `EngineZmqAddresses` contains only resolved endpoints advertised to engines.
- `APIServerProcessManager` transfers one input/output socket pair to each spawned Python frontend. The parent closes each copy immediately after `Process.start()`.
- `RustFrontendProcessManager` passes the HTTP/input/output descriptors, plus the gRPC descriptor when `--grpc-port` is set, with `pass_fds`, then closes the parent ZMQ copies after `Popen`.
- `TransportMode::Bootstrapped` carries the two raw descriptors. Rust validates and consumes each descriptor through `OwnedFd`, then calls zeromq `bind_listener`.
- Ray actors are constructed after the supervisor has bound all frontend listeners, so constructor-time address snapshots already contain real ports.
- The single-process `MPClient` path binds its own `:0` sockets and reads `LAST_ENDPOINT` before launching engines.
- Shutdown terminates frontend processes before closing/unlinking remaining listener resources.

## zeromq dependency

The Rust frontend uses the runtime-neutral listener-adoption API merged in [zeromq/zmq.rs#297](https://github.com/zeromq/zmq.rs/pull/297). No crates.io release contains it yet (latest is `0.6.0`, checked 2026-10-06), so this draft pins upstream `master`:

- repository: [zeromq/zmq.rs](https://github.com/zeromq/zmq.rs)
- revision: [`67dcba97559ebe8e8206dab753710d8b9cb07591`](https://github.com/zeromq/zmq.rs/commit/67dcba97559ebe8e8206dab753710d8b9cb07591)

The API shares the ordinary bind lifecycle and accept loop, keeps async-runtime types internal, preserves monitor events and TCP buffer tuning, and accepts `std::net::TcpListener` / Unix `std::os::unix::net::UnixListener`.

## Local red/green reproduction

I ran a transport-level startup harness matching eight API servers with two TCP endpoints each. It used the host's normal ephemeral allocator and no port squatter.

Red arm: select 16 ports with the old `get_open_port() -> close` sequence, then bind the 16 ZMQ sockets.

Green arm: bind 16 raw listeners with `tcp://127.0.0.1:0`, keep them open, then move them into the 16 ZMQ sockets.

| Arm | Result |
|---|---:|
| probe, close, later ZMQ bind | **1/79 failed** |
| supervisor bind, listener adoption | **79/79 passed** |

The red failure matched #42585:

```text
zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use
(addr='tcp://127.0.0.1:58129', errno=98)
```

The observed rate is workload- and kernel-dependent; this local run demonstrates the same naturally occurring race without deterministic failure injection. The production report in #42585 observed 5/79 full startups.

## Rust frontend red/green validation (2026-10-06)

Ran actual `vllm-rs frontend` subprocesses through each checkout's production address-allocation helper and `RustFrontendProcessManager`:

- **Red:** upstream vLLM main `21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7`, using the probe/release/address-bind path.
- **Green:** this PR at `3fc8ceea4a`, using inherited listeners and upstream zeromq `67dcba97559ebe8e8206dab753710d8b9cb07591`.

The frontend was configured as DP rank 0 of a two-node DP deployment (`data_parallel_size=2`, `data_parallel_size_local=1`), so both frontend ZMQ endpoints are TCP. After supervisor allocation and before Rust launch, a competing TCP socket attempts to bind/listen on the selected frontend endpoint. Tested the input ROUTER and output PULL endpoints independently, five times each.

| Scenario | Red: main | Green: this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Uncontended startup plus HTTP completion | 1/1 passed | 1/1 passed |
| Input-port contention | 5/5 Rust startup failures | 5/5 startup and completion successes |
| Output-port contention | 5/5 Rust startup failures | 5/5 startup and completion successes |

Every red contention trial let the competing socket claim the released port; the Rust process then exited with code 1 and `Address already in use (os error 98)`. Every green trial rejected the competing bind with `EADDRINUSE`, closed the parent's ZMQ descriptor copies after spawn, registered both engines, returned HTTP 200 from `/health`, and returned `OK` with one completion token from `/v1/completions`.

The Rust frontend used cached Qwen3-0.6B model metadata and its real tokenizer. Two protocol-compatible mock engines, built on `vllm_engine_core_client::mock_engine::connect_to_bootstrapped_frontend`, supplied registration and the one-token output; HTTP handling and both ZMQ data paths ran in the actual Rust frontend. Both uncontended controls served the same completion successfully. This deterministic fault-injection experiment establishes the race and its fix; natural failure frequency remains allocator- and workload-dependent. The gRPC listener was not enabled in these runs; its descriptor transfer is covered by the unit test below.

## Validation

Revalidated on 2026-10-06 after merging vLLM main (`21d93d0d8c`). The merge keeps main's Rust gRPC listener inheritance: `RustFrontendProcessManager` passes the gRPC descriptor alongside the HTTP and ZMQ listener descriptors. Tests added on main for gRPC listener inheritance, config-only model selection, and gRPC control capacity now construct inherited listeners instead of frontend bind addresses.

Upstream zeromq:

- `cargo nextest run --test bind_listener` at the pinned revision — 3 passed: TCP adoption and monitor events, IPC adoption and socket-path cleanup, and ordinary hostname binding. (Run on 2026-09-16; the pinned revision is unchanged.)

vLLM Rust (from `rust/`):

- `TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/z54113.XXXX) cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server` — 640 passed, including bootstrapped engine registration, inherited TCP listeners, `frontend_config_adopts_inherited_grpc_listener`, and `control_aggregates_multi_engine_capacity`.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — passed.

vLLM Python (using `/home/bugen/work/vllm/.venv/bin/python` against this worktree):

- `python -m pytest -q tests/utils_/test_network_utils.py tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py -k 'not test_make_zmq_socket_ipv6'` — 32 passed, 1 deselected. The existing IPv6 test binds fixed port 5555, which is occupied on this host. `test_rust_frontend_inherits_grpc_listener` asserts `pass_fds == [http, input, output, grpc]`.
- `RAY_ADDRESS=local python -m pytest -q tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py` — 8 passed, including `test_ray_dp_addresses_resolved_before_actor_creation`.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including ruff, formatting, Python 3.10 mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import, configuration, test-tethering, and Rust manifest/format checks — passed.

Model evaluation: not applicable. The change affects startup transport ownership and does not change inference output.

## AI disclosure

OpenAI Codex and Claude Code assisted with investigation, implementation, testing, review, and drafting. The human submitter must review every changed line and understand and defend the ownership and lifecycle model before requesting maintainer review.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Replace the Torch prefill combine with the shared combine_topk_swa_indices kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

ROCm's V4.1 sparse prefill combines the top-k and sliding-window indices with ordinary Torch indexing, about ninety small ops per call. This sends it to the shared `combine_topk_swa_indices` kernel the CUDA path already uses: one launch, and it brings the SWA bounded-replay bound, the SWA-only guard and the JIT warmup with it. The ROCm-only Triton kernel and the Torch path are removed.

## What changes

- `amd/rocm.py`: prefill calls `combine_topk_swa_indices` from `common/ops/cache_utils.py`.
- The shared kernel gains two guards that leave well-formed input untouched:
  - both lengths clamp at 0. Warmup batches reach it with a negative position, and the Torch path had `clamp_min(0)` for that;
  - a negative top-k index stays -1 instead of becoming `M * b - 1`, a row of the previous request.

## Tests

`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` compares the kernel against the Torch path it replaces, copied over unchanged so the reference cannot drift toward the kernel: `seq_len` below `query_len`, `seq_len == 0`, `compress_ratio == 0`, a non-zero `query_start_loc[0]`, -1 candidates, and windows 64/128/256. It also checks that ROCm dispatches to the shared kernel. `test_v41_combine_topk_swa_stops_at_replay_start` covers the replay bound on that kernel. It runs on ROCm as well, and now includes the shorter replay chunk from #59136 (co-authored by @yuzhouo7), so #59136 is no longer needed.

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py -k stops_at_replay_start
```

```
gfx950 (MI355X)   124 passed, 0 failed
gfx950 (MI355X)     4 passed, 0 failed
```

## Measurements

MI355X, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Both arms run `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0cbac6cd1`; arm B mounts this branch's two source files, so nothing else differs. Each slot is a fresh server with two warm-up rounds and three recorded ones, slots in A B B A order.

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 33792 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 256 \
  --ignore-eos --num-prompts 12 --max-concurrency 2 --seed 42
```

| metric (n=6/arm) | A (main) | B (this PR) | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TTFT median (ms) | 120.7 ± 1.7 | 59.7 ± 1.9 | **−50.5 %** |
| TTFT p99 (ms) | 166.3 ± 2.6 | 81.7 ± 1.3 | **−50.9 %** |
| output throughput (tok/s) | 225.4 ± 0.2 | 234.0 ± 0.2 | +3.8 % |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 8.42 | 8.33 | −1.1 % |

GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k`, 1319 questions, 5-shot): 0.9045 with this branch; main in the same session scored 0.8961 and 0.9067.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Remove WAR for LL CuTeDSL BF16 GEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4772. With it, `mm_bf16(backend="cute-dsl")` falls back to cuBLASLt (with fused bias) when M > 32, and one autotune call profiles both M ranges. This PR removes vLLM's workarounds for the M <= 32 limit of the low-latency CuTeDSL BF16 GEMM, which were added in #50572 and #57285.

## Claims

- `--linear-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` BF16 linears no longer fall back to `F.linear` for M > 32. FlashInfer dispatches them to cuBLASLt with an autotuned algo and fused bias.
- Removes the supplemental 32-token BF16 autotune pass and the `autotune_bf16_only` / `ContextVar` isolation from #57285. The single `max_num_batched_tokens` pass now tunes every BF16 bucket: CuTeDSL for M <= 32, cuBLASLt above.
- Net -77 lines (+16 / -93).

## Validation

Setup: 1x B300 (SM103), torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0.

**Unit tests**: 24 passed.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_flashinfer_bf16_gemm.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -v
```

The existing correctness test gains two cases, M=64 (bias + PDL) and M=512, which cover the FlashInfer cuBLASLt fallback.

commits.pr_title: [Refactor] Abstract DeepGemm MegaMOE backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Refactor DeepGemm MegaMoE integration behind a DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend abstraction to unblock non-SM100 backends; no behavior change on SM100. The DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel is a very high-performance MoE implementation, and is expected to be reused by more models and hardware. For example:
- An equivalent MXFP4 MegaMoE on SM90, where the activation quantization scheme has to change to fit the hardware and different precision requirements.
- Today MXFP4 MoE weights are the default; follow-ups will likely need FP8 and other weight formats on top of the current implementation.

This PR adds an abstract DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend so more models can enable the DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel quickly, and so external vLLM plugins can support more scenarios flexibly.

Main changes:
- DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend currently exposes transform_weights (routed / shared), bf16_mega_gate, run_mega_moe, supports_shared_experts, and supports_bf16_mega_gate; it also abstracts mma_type and the hidden-state activation scheme.
- The existing DeepGEMM usage in DeepSeek V4 and Kimi K3 is moved into DeepGemmSm100MegaMoEBackend, keeping the implementation completely unchanged.
- prepare_megamoe_inputs is extended to support a new quantization mode fp8 with group_k=128 and fp32 scales.

## Test Plan
- On SM100, the code logic is unchanged, including DeepGemmSm100MegaMoEBackend and prepare_megamoe_inputs.
- Test DeepGEMM MegaMoE variant on SM90.

## Test Result
Run TP4+EP on hopper works correctly.
```
INFO 09-21 11:29:57 [__init__.py:90] [vllm_hopper_mega_moe] registered SM90 MegaMoE backend (DeepGemmSm90MegaMoEBackend) for DeepSeek V4.
INFO 09-21 11:29:57 [__init__.py:90] [vllm_hopper_mega_moe] registered SM90 MegaMoE backend (DeepGemmSm90MegaMoEBackend) for DeepSeek V4
```

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Use native merge_attn_states kernel on gfx942/gfx950
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Use the native `merge_attn_states` kernel on CDNA3 and newer (gfx942, gfx950, gfx1250) instead of the Triton fallback. The kernel is already built and registered on ROCm. The Python dispatch in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/merge_attn_states.py` is gated on `get_cdna_version() >= 3`, so gfx90a stays on Triton. The kernel was introduced for CUDA in #16173.

## Claims

- On gfx942 and gfx950, the native kernel is faster than the Triton kernel in every case of `tests/kernels/attention/test_merge_attn_states.py`: 2592 timed cases per GPU, median 2.4x, minimum 1.1x.
- The native output matches Triton on both architectures, including FP8 output (`float8_e4m3fnuz` on gfx942, `float8_e4m3fn` on gfx950).
- In end-to-end serving of an MLA model, the merge kernel time drops about 4x. Serving metrics are unchanged within run-to-run noise, because merge is a small share of prefill.
- gfx90a (CDNA2) and RDNA stay on Triton. `get_cdna_version() >= 3` also selects gfx1250 (CDNA5); that GPU was not part of the runs below.

## Validation

### Unit test

`pytest -s tests/kernels/attention/test_merge_attn_states.py`, unmodified, on one GPU at vLLM 92044241:

| GPU | arch | result | native vs Triton, 2592 timed cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MI325X | gfx942 | 2598 passed | min 1.10x, median 2.39x, max 8.58x, 0 slower |
| MI355X | gfx950 | 2598 passed | min 1.64x, median 2.36x, max 8.30x, 0 slower |

The test calls the native op and the Triton op directly, so these numbers do not depend on this change. The smallest gains on both GPUs are fp32 inputs at head size 256.

The rows from #16173 (16 query heads per rank, head size 128, i.e. an MLA model at TP=8):

| tokens | dtype | MI325X triton | MI325X native | MI325X speedup | MI355X triton | MI355X native | MI355X speedup |

| 613 | float32 | 0.03099ms | 0.01465ms | 2.1154x | 0.02969ms | 0.01297ms | 2.2890x |
| 1024 | float32 | 0.03445ms | 0.01525ms | 2.2584x | 0.03188ms | 0.01413ms | 2.2568x |
| 1536 | float32 | 0.03907ms | 0.01745ms | 2.2395x | 0.03794ms | 0.01573ms | 2.4125x |
| 4096 | float32 | 0.06322ms | 0.03733ms | 1.6936x | 0.06578ms | 0.02589ms | 2.5406x |
| 256 | float16 | 0.02821ms | 0.01287ms | 2.1911x | 0.02721ms | 0.01329ms | 2.0466x |

With FP8 output (same rows, bf16/fp16/fp32 input to FP8), native is 2.1x to 2.9x faster on MI325X and 2.2x to 3.5x faster on MI355X.

### End-to-end

Kimi-K3, 8x MI355X, TP=8, FP8 KV cache, `--load-format dummy`, concurrency 16. Each configuration was run once without and once with this change; nothing else differs between the two runs. All numbers are from the profiled runs. Merge launches and merge kernel time come from the rank-0 torch profiler trace over the same window of steps, which covers one full request. TTFT, TPOT and throughput are from the same runs, with the profiler active for that window.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reland #53020: tie lm_head.weight for Nemotron Parse when checkpoint omits it
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Re-lands #53020 (commit `83cadd65d9`), reverted in #59805. The diff is byte-identical to the reverted commit (`git patch-id` matches). Original bug report: #53019. Supersedes #60266, which carries the same diff; thanks @DiegoCao for preparing it.

`NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration` builds a standalone `ParallelLMHead` and only populates it from `lm_head.*` weights. A checkpoint that sets `tie_word_embeddings` and ships no `lm_head.weight`, such as `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0`, therefore keeps a randomly initialized output head. Nothing reports it: the server starts, reports healthy, and returns garbage.

## Why this can land now

#59805 did not revert because the fix was wrong. It reverted because the `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` case added to `test_nemotron_parse.py` failed in the nightly full CI run while loading that checkpoint's tokenizer, before any model code ran:

```
transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:120 in convert_to_native_format
    local_kwargs["tokenizer_object"] = TokenizerFast.from_file(fast_tokenizer_file)
E   Exception: DuplicatePatternError: [225, 131, 156] at line 449472 column 1
```

The cause was the CI pin `tokenizers==0.23.1`. The 2.0 `tokenizer.json` uses an NFKC normalizer, and 14 pairs of its added tokens become identical after normalization (for example `ნ` U+10DC and `ჼ` U+10FC both normalize to `e1 83 9c`, the `[225, 131, 156]` in the error). 0.23.1 rejects the duplicates when it builds its matcher; 0.23.2 (daachorse 1.0.1 → 3.0.0, huggingface/tokenizers#2050) accepts them. #59796 bumped the pin.

| | PR | merged (UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| fix | #53020 | 2026-10-01 16:26 |
| revert | #59805 | 2026-10-02 17:19 |
| tokenizer bump that unblocks it | #59796 | 2026-10-02 18:33 |

`Tokenizer.from_file` on the 2.0 `tokenizer.json`, by `tokenizers` version:

| 0.22.2 | **0.23.1** | 0.23.2 | 1.0.0rc2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| loads | **`DuplicatePatternError`** | loads | loads |

Under the current CI pins (`tokenizers==0.23.2`, `transformers==5.18.0`), `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0")` loads (`TokenizersBackend`, vocab 72,249).

## Test Plan

- `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_nemotron_parse.py::test_models`: the `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` parametrization is restored. It is the only coverage of the tied-head path and is the case that must be green before merge.
- That test runs in `Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)`, which is `optional: true`, so it did not run on #53020's PR CI and only surfaced in the nightly run. Could a maintainer include that step when triggering CI here?
- `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-v1.2` stays in the same parametrization and is unaffected (see below).

## Test Result

Out-of-CI validation on one RTX 6000 Ada, serving the 2.0 checkpoint with `vllm serve … --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}'`, one greedy request (50 max tokens) with the model's documented control-token prompt on the deterministic test image from the model repo's `test_golden.py`:

| build | output |
|---|---|
| vLLM v0.30.0 without this patch | `<s><s><s>…` (50 × `<s>`) |
| **v0.30.0 with this patch** | `<x_0.3906><y_0.5969>\begin{tabular}{ccccc}\n\end{tabular}<x_0.6084><y_0.6367><class_Table>` |

The patched output is byte-identical to what the model's own shipped workaround (`vllm_tied_patch/sitecustomize.py` in the HF repo) produces on the same input.

Why v1.2 cannot be affected: the two checkpoints differ exactly where the new branch reads.

| checkpoint | `tie_word_embeddings` (config / `config.decoder`) | `lm_head.weight` in checkpoint | tensors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-v1.2` | `false` / `false` | present | 667 |
| `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` | `true` / `true` | absent | 666 |

The tie goes through `ParallelLMHead.tie_weights()`, so it routes via `quant_method.tie_weights` rather than assigning `.weight` directly.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both files.

## Notes

- Commit trailers preserve the original authorship (`Signed-off-by: Anish Kumar`, `Co-authored-by: Cyrus Leung`).
- Root-cause write-up on the original PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53020#issuecomment-5957763325.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Declare max_tp_shards on the DSpark MLA KV cache spec
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes a Kimi-K3 + DSpark perf regression from #57652: the K3 DSpark draft's `MLAAttentionSpec` does not declare `max_tp_shards`, so its MLA layers stop merging with the target's and the KV cache splits from **4 to 20 groups**. One-line fix: declare `max_tp_shards=1` on the draft spec, matching `MLAAttention`.

## Claims

- Restores Kimi-K3 + DSpark to 4 KV cache groups (20 on current `main`).
- Recovers the regression: **+3.7% total throughput/GPU, −3.3% median TPOT** vs. current nightly on MI355X TP8, matching both the pre-#57652 nightly and a full revert of #57652.
- Restores the pre-#57652 GPU KV pool size (3,192,149 → 3,274,215 tokens).
- Keeps #57652's offloading change; no behavior change for K3's offloading `kv_tp_replicas` (KDA layers already pin the gcd to 1).

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py::test_k3_dspark_mla_kv_cache_spec_groups_with_target_mla`): builds the target spec via `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` and the draft spec via the K3 `MultiHeadLatentAttention.get_kv_cache_spec`, then groups 24 target + 5 draft layers with `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size`.
- Without the fix: `AssertionError: assert 6 == 1`
- With the fix: passes (1 group, 29 layers)

Run inside `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-ac9126e5…` with `python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py -k k3_dspark_mla_kv_cache_spec`. `pre-commit` passes on both files.

**End-to-end**: Kimi-K3 (MXFP4) + Kimi-K3-DSpark, MI355X ×8, TP8, exact InferenceX CI serve command (DSpark k=7 synthetic AL 3.84, fp8 KV, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, FULL cudagraph, `--max-num-seqs 16`). Client: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 80`, 3 seeds per arm after a 16-prompt warmup, same host, arms run back to back.

| image | KV cache groups | total tput/GPU (tok/s) | output tput (tok/s) | median TPOT (ms) | median ITL (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| nightly `36768d1` (before #57652) | 4 | 729 | 648 | 11.13 | 33.4 |
| nightly `ac9126e` (includes #57652) | 20 | 701 | 623 | 11.47 | 34.4 |
| `ac9126e` + revert #57652 | 4 | 726 | 646 | 11.15 | 33.2 |
| **`ac9126e` + this PR** | **4** | **727** | **647** | **11.09** | **33.1** |

Per-seed median TPOT for this PR: 11.10 / 10.99 / 11.18 ms (vs 11.43 / 11.44 / 11.54 without it). The regression was first seen in InferenceX CI on the K3 agentic c8 cell (`kimik3 fp4 mi355x vllm TP8 mtp dram KV offload vllm-simple c8`): −6.1% total throughput/GPU and −16.6% p90 interactivity between the two nightlies.

**Accuracy (gsm8k)**: same server config but with real DSpark verification (`"rejection_sample_method": "block"`, no synthetic acceptance length), evaluated with the InferenceX CI lm-eval setup: `lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template --tasks gsm8k` (5-shot, CI task YAML), full 1319-question test set, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=16384`, `num_concurrent=16`.

| image | KV cache groups | gsm8k exact_match (strict / flexible) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `ac9126e` + this PR | 4 | 0.9636 ± 0.0052 / 0.9636 ± 0.0052 |

Mean DSpark acceptance length during the eval was ~3.0, confirming real verification.

## Details

**Root cause.** #57652 added `AttentionSpec.max_tp_shards` and set it to `1` in `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec`. `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py` (used for the K3 target on NVIDIA and for the DSpark draft on both vendors) builds its own `MLAAttentionSpec` and leaves it `None`. On ROCm the K3 target uses `MLAAttention` (`1`) while the draft uses this class (`None`), so `MLAAttentionSpec.merge`'s per-field `AttentionSpec` equality check rejects them. `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` then sees buckets of 69 KDA / 24 target MLA / 5 draft MLA layers instead of 69 / 29, the group size drops from 29 to 5, and the group count goes from 4 (3 KDA + 1 MLA) to 20 (14 + 5 + 1). The server log shows `kv cache group sizes` growing from 4 to 20 entries and `Add 1 padding layers` twice instead of `Add 18 padding layers`.

**Why 20 groups is slower.** `_build_attention_metadata` builds per KV cache group each step, and neither the ROCm K3 KDA builder nor the AITER MLA builder supports `update_block_table` reuse, so every extra group is a full `builder.build()` plus its own block-table/slot-mapping work.

**Why `1` is correct.** The draft's MLA latent KV has a single head and is replicated across TP ranks, same as `MLAAttention`. On NVIDIA the target and draft both go from `None` to `1`, so they still merge and grouping does not change. `kv_tp_replicas` remains 1 for K3 because its KDA (Mamba) layers contribute 1 to the gcd, so offloading behavior is unchanged.

**Not duplicate.** No open PR sets `max_tp_shards` on the K3 draft spec. #57942 (draft) adds a separate AMD DSpark MLA module, and #58207 changes the group-size heuristic. Both are broader and neither fixes this mismatch on `main`. This PR is the minimal fix for the regression.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Map sleep-mode cuMem memory for the host
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm ≥ 7.2, any `Tensor.item()` on sleep-mode (cuMem pool) memory segfaults. As a result, every FP8 checkpoint with `enable_sleep_mode=True` crashes during `process_weights_after_loading`. This PR maps the pool for the host as well, as PyTorch already does for its own VMM memory, and re-enables the FP8 sleep test on ROCm. That test was skipped as "Segfaults on ROCm." in #57163.

## Claims

- FP8 models start and sleep/wake with `enable_sleep_mode` on ROCm. Before this change they segfaulted at startup with AITER on or off, e.g. Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 on MI300X.
- `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales` runs on ROCm again and passes.
- The CUDA path is unchanged, and the fix adds no measurable cost to allocation or wake.

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-bb87d227` (ROCm 7.2, torch 2.13), with only `cumem_allocator.cpp` rebuilt. The file is identical between that commit and this branch's base.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales` (skip removed) | fails: worker segfault in `_local_scalar_dense_cuda` | passes |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8, `enable_sleep_mode`, TP1 | segfault at `kv_cache.py:169` (`layer.q_scale > 0.0`) | starts; greedy output bit-exact over 2 cycles × (level-1 full, level-1 selective, level-2 + `reload_weights`) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-FP8, `enable_sleep_mode`, TP2 | segfault at startup | starts; bit-exact over level-1 full, level-1 selective, level-2 + `reload_weights` |
| `.item()` on a cuMem tensor (offset 0 / 300 / 700 MiB into a 1 GiB segment) | segfault | correct value |
| `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` | — | 19 passed, 2 skipped (graph-pool tests are CUDA-only on main) |
| 100 GiB `kv_cache` allocation: first map / first wake | 0.085–0.089 s / 0.096–0.121 s | 0.098–0.102 s / 0.097 s |

MI355X (gfx950), same image, amdgpu 6.16.6, AITER on:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales` (skip removed) | fails: worker segfault | passes |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8, `enable_sleep_mode`, TP1 | segfault at startup | starts; sane output with no NaN logprobs over 2 cycles × (level-1 full, level-1 selective, level-2 + `reload_weights`). Exact match isn't meaningful here, because with AITER the output varies run to run even while awake. |

Repeated wakes of the same 100 GiB slow to about 1 s in both builds, which points to the driver still wiping the previously released memory, not to this change.

`pre-commit` passes. The re-enabled test runs in the existing ":amd: (MI300) Basic Correctness Sleep Mode" step (`basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode`).

## Details

**Root cause.** On ROCm ≥ 7.2, `_local_scalar_dense_cuda` (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/CUDAScalar.cu`) has a large-BAR fast path. It syncs the stream and dereferences the device pointer from the host. The path is taken when `isLargeBar` is set and the tensor's deleter is the caching allocator's `raw_deleter`. That's true for vLLM's pluggable cuMem pool too, because it is wrapped by the caching allocator.

The fast path relies on the device memory also being mapped for the CPU. That holds for `hipMalloc` memory on a large-BAR part. It doesn't hold for a `hipMemCreate` + `hipMemMap` mapping whose access was granted only to the device, which is what `create_and_map` did, so the host read segfaults. PyTorch's own VMM path (`ExpandableSegment::setAccess`) adds a `hipMemLocationTypeHost` access descriptor under the same `ROCM_VERSION >= 70200` gate, which is why `expandable_segments` never crashes. This change mirrors that.

I confirmed the mechanism with a standalone HIP program. With device-only access, a host dereference segfaults for every size, chunking and alignment I tried (2 MiB to 1 GiB, 256 MiB chunks). Adding the host descriptor makes the dereference succeed.

**Why FP8.** `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading` calls `layer.q_scale > 0.0`, which is an `.item()` on a parameter allocated in the sleep-mode `weights` pool. It is simply the first `.item()` that runs on sleep-mode memory at startup. Any other `.item()` on that memory would crash the same way.

**Scope.** Only ROCm builds with `HIP_VERSION >= 7.2` change. On CUDA and older ROCm, a single device descriptor is passed exactly as before. The host mapping applies at first allocation and on every wake, since both go through `create_and_map`. It uses no extra memory.

**Limitations.** Validated on gfx942 and gfx950. Like PyTorch, the host descriptor is added unconditionally rather than only on large-BAR devices; I haven't checked small-BAR parts.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept successful 2xx responses for batch output uploads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Batch result uploads treat successful HTTP 201/204 responses as failures, upload the same output five times, then raise. Accept 2xx responses in both memory and file upload paths.

## Claims

- Successful PUT responses complete after one upload, without retry sleeps.
- Error responses retain the existing retry count and response-body diagnostics.

## Validation

A focused harness loads upload_data directly from the checked-out source by AST extraction against a real local aiohttp PUT server, with real file and request-body I/O. Only retry sleep is replaced.

Before: HTTP 201/204 each caused five PUTs and an exception, in both upload paths.
After: 10/10 HTTP cases passed: 200/201/204 succeed once, 400/500 retain five attempts and error details, each from memory and file. Seven exact-source unit cases also pass under AST isolation.

Local workspace-only harness command (the harness is not included in this PR): `.venv/Scripts/python.exe ../validate_batch_upload.py`.

This does not claim a full run-batch engine run or native pytest pass. Native test collection requires the unavailable vLLM runtime dependencies.

Native regression command for a fully installed development environment (not yet passed locally): `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k upload_data -q`.

Ruff 0.14.0 check/format, git diff --check, and applicable pre-commit hooks (including mypy 3.10/3.12 and test/CI tethering) pass. Windows required UTF-8 mode and Git Bash in PATH. The unrelated Dockerfile graph updater was skipped; no Dockerfile changed. Existing Buildkite benchmark and entrypoints launchers suites include these test files.

## Details

The existing success condition accepted only status 200. RFC 9110 section 9.3.4 defines successful PUT responses including 201 and 204: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-9.3.4 . Azure Put Blob returns 201: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/put-blob .

Duplicate checks: open PR searches for upload_data, upload 204, 2xx, and upload batch found no matching fix. AI assistance: Codex assisted analysis, implementation, and validation.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Pick the DP world-group port at bind time via the coordination store
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `--data-parallel-size N`, the DP world group's rendezvous port comes from `_data_parallel_master_port_list` — probed once at config time and consumed by `get_next_dp_init_port()` when the engines finally call `init_process_group`, **minutes later** (after worker spawn, CUDA init, and model load). Nothing holds the port in between, so any other process — most commonly a sibling vLLM instance cold-starting on the same host, the standard shape in RL rollout fleets — can take it. Startup then fails at its very last step with the engines hanging on:

```
(Worker pid=...) torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to
listen on any local network address. port: <n>, ... EADDRINUSE
```

#36330 fixed exactly this defect for the elastic-EP stateless groups: rank 0 binds an ephemeral port, keeps the listening socket, and publishes the port through a coordination TCPStore. This PR extends that mechanism to the last remaining pre-allocated consumer, the world group:

- `launch_core_engines()` creates the coordination store for online DP (dp>1, engine rank 0 local; the initial MoE-only gate was removed in a follow-up commit, see below) when none exists yet, and hands its port to engines through the existing startup handshake (`_coord_store_port`).
- `init_distributed_environment()`: for the DP path, group rank 0 creates the world-group TCPStore on port 0 — the kernel assigns the port and the store owns it from birth — then publishes the resulting port via the coordination store; other ranks read it and connect. All ranks pass the store to `init_process_group` (`store=` argument), so the port is never released between choice and use. Without a coord store the previous behavior is unchanged.

## Design notes for reviewers

Answers to the questions this diff naturally raises.

**Why publish through a TCPStore rather than the handshake or spawn args.** The port does not exist until group rank 0 binds — after every engine has spawned and after the handshake replies have gone out (the frontend replies to each HELLO as it arrives; rank 0 has not bound yet at that point). Delivery therefore needs a channel that (a) works after all startup messages, (b) blocks until the value appears (ranks reach group init in arbitrary order), and (c) is reachable from both consumer levels: EngineCore processes (DP gloo group, store-based since #36330) and workers (world group), which have no handshake connection to the frontend at all. A key-value store with blocking `get` is the smallest thing satisfying all three, and #36330 already built it — this PR only extends where it is created (MP path, before the Ray branch) and adds one consumer.

**Why rank 0 creates the store on port 0 and reads the port back.** Ownership must never gap: the world-group TCPStore itself binds port 0, owns the kernel-assigned port from birth, and `.port` reads it back for publication — the same readback pattern the coordination store (and zmq's `LAST_ENDPOINT`) already uses. The already-bound store is then passed to `init_process_group` via `store=`; torch requires `store` and `init_method` to be mutually exclusive, hence `init_method=None if world_pg_store else distributed_init_method` at both call sites. Rank 0 passes `wait_for_workers=False` because workers can only connect after the port is published, so the master cannot block for them inside its own constructor; PG init synchronizes through store keys as usual. An earlier revision of this PR bound a raw socket manually and handed it to `TCPStore(master_listen_fd=...)`; review simplified it to `TCPStore(port=0)` — same invariant, one layer less, and it drops the fd-adoption/libuv compat surface (cf. the `use_libuv=False` pin in `StatelessProcessGroup.create` for pytorch#150215).

**An externally-built store is equivalent to the torch-built one.** The constructor arguments mirror torch's own `_create_c10d_store` (`world_size`, `is_master=(rank == 0)`, group timeout, `multi_tenant=True`); both paths converge in `_new_process_group_helper`, which cannot tell who built the store. `store=` is the public contract torchelastic uses in production. Two known differences, both benign: (1) `wait_for_workers=False` on rank 0 (see above) moves a missing-worker failure from store-construction timeout to PG-init rendezvous timeout — the behavior torchelastic deployments already run with; (2) torch wraps rendezvous-built stores in `PrefixStore("default_pg")` but takes a passed store raw — harmless because the store is freshly created and dedicated to this group, and all members take the same branch.

**Store-creation guards.** Each condition excludes a deployment where creating the store would be useless or wrong: `dp_size > 1` (no consumer otherwise), `not offline_mode` (scope: offline keeps existing behavior), `dp_rank == 0 and local_engine_count > 0` (the store must bind on the DP master node; an API-server-only frontend would `bind()` an IP that is not its own), `not enable_elastic_ep` (the Ray actor manager creates its own store later, unchanged from #36330). An earlier idempotency check on `_coord_store_port` was dropped: no in-tree writer can set the field before this block runs.

**Fallback path is byte-for-byte the old behavior.** With `_coord_store_port` unset (offline, external launcher / SPMD, elastic, or an older frontend during version skew), `world_pg_store` stays `None` and both changed call sites degrade to their previous form.

**How the store address travels.** One field added to the existing handshake copy-list covers remote (headless) MP engines; local engines receive it in the config at spawn, Ray actors in the actor-constructor config, and workers inherit it when the executor spawns them. Non-MoE MP engines are rewritten to independent dp=1 (`reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank`) and never consume the store; the non-MoE case that needs it is the Ray DP backend (no such rewrite), which is covered via the actor-constructor config.

**Lifetimes.** The coordination store lives on the `launch_core_engines()` frame, which runs `wait_for_engine_startup()` after its yield — so it stays alive exactly until all engines are ready, then is discarded. The world group's own rendezvous TCPStore is a separate, process-lifetime object. The two are deliberately not merged: reusing the coordination store as the group's rendezvous store would make the frontend process a runtime dependency of every engine collective.

## Reproduction & A/B results

Hardware: single GB200 node (aarch64, 4 GPUs), image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (2026-08-04). Arm "fixed" = same image with this patch applied. Model: a 9-layer MoE test checkpoint with dummy weights (`--load-format dummy`); any small MoE reproduces, e.g. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`.

Two experiments, all rounds on identical images/configs:

1. **Deterministic squatter**: start `vllm serve <moe> -dp 4 -tp 1` with `VLLM_PORT` set (making the config-time probe deterministic); a squatter process waits until the EngineCore processes exist (probe done, world-group bind not yet) and then binds-and-holds `[VLLM_PORT, VLLM_PORT+16)`:

   ```python
   # squat.py — run alongside the server, after EngineCore appears in its log
   import socket, time
   socks = []
   for p in range(42000, 42016):
       s = socket.socket(); s.bind(("0.0.0.0", p)); s.listen(); socks.append(s)
   time.sleep(600)
   ```

2. **Concurrent cold start (RL shape, no artificial interference)**: two `-dp 2 -tp 1` instances on one node, same `VLLM_PORT`, started simultaneously.

| experiment | main | with this fix |
|---|---|---|
| squatter | **6/6 startup failure** (EADDRINUSE at world-group init, process hangs) | **8/8 healthy** (full band squatted) |
| concurrent cold start | **6/6 startup failure** | **6/6 healthy** (both instances) |

The failure mode on main matches field reports: the server does not exit — it hangs after minutes of model loading, which is the expensive way to fail.

## Relationship to existing work

- **#36330** (merged) introduced the coordination-store mechanism and fixed the stateless-group half of this defect; this PR completes the class by migrating the world group. Same defect statement, same cure.
- Related symptom reports: #39015 (EADDRINUSE on 29500-family defaults), #28498 (port-conflict tracker), #14919.
- Sibling PRs for other port-race sites: #50960 (zmq shm broadcast, merged), #50965 (`get_open_port` reserved-range livelock, merged), #50969 (Ray executor TCPStore host), #50999 (single-node executor `file://` rendezvous).
- Duplicate-work check: [open PRs touching dp master port](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+data_parallel_master_port), [open PRs mentioning 39015](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+39015+in%3Abody) — none migrate the world group to the coordination store.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_dp_world_group_port.py tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py -k "world_group or coordination_store"
```

- A/B experiments above (deterministic + statistical, 26 rounds total, zero exceptions).
- Existing DP suites (`tests/v1/test_async_llm_dp.py`, distributed tests) exercise the changed init path end to end; behavior without a coord store is unchanged by construction.

## Test Result

- See table above; `pre-commit` clean on the changed files (the forbidden-import hook's `pickle` flag on `parallel_state.py` is its pre-existing allowlisted import surfacing under a worktree path prefix).

## AI Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, the A/B experiments, and drafting this description. Opened as a draft for the submitter's final line-by-line review before requesting maintainer review.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Reproduced nightly A/B (2026-08-07)

Actual run: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on h200-0 (baseline, image `sha256:40e504de…`) and h200-1 (PR head, image `sha256:928dde7d…`), each with 8× H200. The repro calls `init_distributed_environment()` with the same coordinated-online-DP branch this PR changes. A squatter binds the exact port returned by the baseline `get_next_dp_init_port()` after its probe socket closes and before `init_process_group()` starts.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| base `24c939c47d` | `torch.distributed.DistNetworkError`: `EADDRINUSE` while TCPStore listens |
| PR head `ad4aec4ed` | passes: rank 0 binds `:0`, creates the TCPStore from that held socket, then initializes the world group |

To reproduce: checkout base/head, run the same nightly image with `--network host`; set `data_parallel_size=2`, inject a `get_next_dp_init_port()` that returns a port a background `socket.bind()+listen()` has just claimed, and call `init_distributed_environment(world_size=1, rank=0, backend="gloo")`. The base follows `tcp://<squatted-port>` and fails; the head uses `_coord_store_port` and succeeds. This is deterministic rather than a timing-only cold-start test.

## Non-MoE DP completion (2026-08-07)

The original coordination-store creation was incorrectly gated on `model_config.is_moe`.  This misses ordinary replicated DP models: `init_distributed_environment()` still creates the DP-expanded world group whenever `data_parallel_size > 1`, so it fell back to the pre-allocated `_data_parallel_master_port_list` and retained the exact probe-to-bind race.

Deterministic nightly A/B (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`) on both h200-0 and h200-1 uses production `launch_core_engines()` with a non-MoE DP=2 config and a fake process manager.  PR head `ad4aec4ed` fails `AssertionError: non-MoE DP did not receive a coordination TCPStore`; commit `2827357fb7` passes on both hosts: `PASS non-MoE DP received a coordination TCPStore`.  The added focused pytest passes, and ruff, mypy-3.10, and full changed-file pre-commit pass.

The change removes only the MoE gate; all online local rank-0 DP launches now retain the coordination TCPStore until EngineCore startup, allowing rank 0 to bind-and-hold the actual world-group listener before publishing its port.

## Real GPU serving validation (2026-08-07)

On h200-0, mounted the PR head into `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` and ran `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 18018 --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size-local 2 --data-parallel-rpc-port 0 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --enforce-eager` on two H200 GPUs. Both non-MoE DP EngineCores initialized, the API reached `GET /v1/models` (200), and `POST /v1/completions` returned a completion. This exercises the same non-MoE DP launch branch protected by commit `2827357fb7`.

## Fresh non-MoE nightly confirmation (2026-08-07)

After the follow-up commit `2827357fb7`, h200-1 re-ran production `launch_core_engines()` for non-MoE, MP DP=2 in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (head `sha256:928dde7d…`, `--gpus all --network host`). The current head printed `PASS non-MoE DP received a coordination TCPStore`. This confirms the rebase/current branch still covers the non-MoE variant that `ad4aec4ed` initially omitted.

## port=0 simplification validation (2026-08-08)

Commit `613d35eacf` replaces the manual socket bind/listen/detach + `TCPStore(master_listen_fd=...)` handoff with `TCPStore(port=0)` + `.port` readback (review suggestion). Validated by driving the real modified `init_distributed_environment()` in two spawned processes (dp=2 config with `_coord_store_port` set): rank 0 created the world-group store on a kernel-assigned port and published it, rank 1 read it from the coordination store and connected, `init_process_group(store=)` formed the 2-rank world group, and a gloo `all_reduce` returned `[2.0, 2.0]` with clean exits. ruff check/format pass. The earlier GPU serving validation predates this commit; it should be repeated before undrafting.

## Test coverage (2026-10-06)

Two tests, both CPU-only (gloo), run as part of `pytest v1/engine`:

- `tests/v1/engine/test_dp_world_group_port.py`: two spawned processes bring up a DP=2 world group with the pre-allocated port already taken by another socket. With a coordination store the group binds its own port and both ranks all-reduce correctly; without one the pre-allocated path still works. Checked against unpatched `main`: the taken-port case fails with `EADDRINUSE` on the pre-allocated port, the fallback case passes. On this branch both pass (27 s).
- `test_coordination_store_held_only_by_the_online_dp_master` (rewritten from the earlier non-MoE test): a table over launch configurations. The online DP master holds a reachable store for both the mp and ray backends; non-master nodes, offline mode, elastic EP and single-engine deployments do not. Against unpatched `main` the two "holds a store" cases fail and the four "no store" cases pass.

## MI355 CI failure (build 93141) and fix (2026-10-07)

`:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP Extended` hung for 30 minutes in `test_async_llm_dp.py` with DP=2/TP=2 on both attempts, while the L4 run of the same step passed. In each attempt one worker of the DP-rank-1 engine never reached the world-group init: it was stuck on the coordination store (`wait timeout ... keys: /world_pg_port` in the retry), and its three peers then waited 30 minutes on its gloo key.

Root cause: `get_cached_tcp_store_client` caches one connected client per process. `DPEngineCoreProc` populates it in `_init_data_parallel` before it creates the executor, so with the default fork start method every worker inherited the same connected socket, and the two TP siblings of one engine interleaved their requests on it. The L4 run of the same step shows no spawn override either, so it forks as well; whether the interleaving corrupts the stream depends on whether the siblings' requests overlap, and that run did not hit it. The hazard is therefore not ROCm specific. This PR is the first to read the coordination store from workers at init, so the latent cache issue surfaced here.

Fix: the port exchange needs the store once per worker, so it now opens its own short-lived client instead of the process-wide cached one. The cached client itself is still not fork-safe for its other callers (elastic EP); that is pre-existing and left for a follow-up.
