commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Restore KVCR construction through the secondary-tier factory
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58087.

A standard `type="kvcr"` secondary tier fails to initialize because `SecondaryTierFactory` passes `backpressure_detector=None` even when backpressure is not configured, while `KVCRSecondaryTierManager` does not accept that argument. Consequently, the server exits before it can serve a request.

Accept the optional detector in the KVCR constructor and forward it to `SecondaryTierManager`. Keep the parameter at the end of the existing signature to preserve existing positional arguments. Route the existing KVCR test helper through the production factory and exercise request/load behavior with both default and explicitly configured backpressure.

This restores the constructor contract introduced by [#50045](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50045) after the KVCR adapter landed in [#53624](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53624). Default configurations retain a `None` detector; explicitly configured detectors are preserved rather than silently discarded.

Duplicate checks on 2026-09-22 found no existing issue or PR addressing this constructor mismatch. [#57500](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57500) concerns buffer lifetime after a native startup failure and leaves this signature unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run the focused suites with the optional KVCR package installed:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_backpressure.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py -q
```

The adapted KVCR tests use the real factory with the existing recording backend. They cover construction, configured detector retention, request hints, key/descriptor translation, load completion, and request cleanup.

Changed-file checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/kvcr/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/kvcr/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
```

For serving validation, repeat the accompanying issue's Qwen3-0.6B startup command on the same RTX 3090 and send three deterministic `/v1/completions` requests. Compare their generated token IDs with the primary-only reference. Run the repository's required checks on the changed files.

## Test Result

The published fix is commit `ab62868f6f16b4b21ced4655150833100a07cb83`. Its patch is byte-for-byte identical to the validated two-file patch.

Before the production fix, on vLLM source `c723a831a81cb4ff89ea6d61b2d15109306ed1bc`:

- The KVCR suite with its helper routed through the production factory failed all 21 cases with the constructor keyword error.
- The generation-only GPU reproduction with real Qwen3-0.6B weights exited during startup with the same `TypeError`.
- The primary-only control started successfully and returned HTTP 200 for all three completion requests, each generating `[7407, 304, 279, 3283, 315, 12095, 13, 362]`.

Environment: KVCR `0.1.0` at `317e62f301300c101bf9c911e020fb89b35f1583`, NIXL `1.3.2`, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, Transformers `5.16.1`, RTX 3090, FP16. The editable vLLM checkout uses the official cu130 native artifacts from `e9f169d16b9408bb9ae44f75072b91a5521d733c`; the changes between that revision and the tested source contain no C/C++/CUDA source changes. Distribution metadata still reads `0.1.dev648+g1fee69838.precompiled`, while Python source is the `c723a831` checkout plus this patch.

After the fix:

- All six related suites above: **229 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** in 85.55 seconds, including all 21 KVCR cases. There were 14 existing PyTorch deprecation warnings.
- The same real-weight GPU configuration started successfully with the real KVCR/NIXL UCX backend. All three completion requests returned HTTP 200; generated token IDs, corresponding per-token logprobs, prompt token IDs, and finish reasons matched the primary-only reference exactly.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed. The manual Python 3.12 mypy check passed as well. `git diff --check` passed.

At submission, the affected constructor, factory, base class, and KVCR tests remain unchanged at upstream `496c6472cb70d5eb8681dadae238d160f5086454`. The test results above use the stated `c723a831` baseline plus this patch.

The single-GPU serving check measures startup and generation. It does not establish cross-node transfer correctness or a broad model-quality evaluation.

---

OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, implementation, and execution of the validation reported above.

commits.pr_title: [UX] Skip checkpoint shards an MTP head does not load
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MTP heads load from their target's checkpoint, so loaders that read whole files (InstantTensor, fastsafetensors, multi-thread, eager/prefetch) read the entire checkpoint a second time, only for the head's `load_weights` to drop almost all of it. This PR lets a model say which checkpoint weights it does not load, and `DefaultModelLoader` drops the safetensors shards that hold nothing else before any loader opens them.

Related: #58016 adds a similar model hook for per-tensor skipping in the lazy safetensors path (see Details).

## Claims

- With `--load-format instanttensor`, the MTP drafter no longer re-reads the target checkpoint: 704 G → 20 G on GLM-5.3, 149 G → 3.35 G on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 61.3 G → 10.2 G on Nemotron-3.5-Lightning.
- Total model load time drops accordingly: 226.5 s → 127.5 s (GLM-5.3, TP=8), 56.5 s → 36.6 s (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=2), 22.8 s → 14.9 s (Nemotron, 1 GPU).
- Generated text and draft acceptance are unchanged.
- Opted in: DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA), DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 (NVIDIA and ROCm), Nemotron-H, Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next MTP heads. Models without the hook are unaffected.

## Validation

End to end on 8x H200, local XFS, InstantTensor 0.2.0, one run per configuration:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --load-format instanttensor --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' [--tensor-parallel-size N]
```

| Model | Drafter read, before → after | Shards read | Drafter load | Total model load | Draft tokens accepted, before / after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zai-org/GLM-5.3`, TP=8 | 704 G → 20.0 G | 4 of 141 | 109.9 s → 3.4 s | 226.5 s → 127.5 s | 54 of 65 / 54 of 65 |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP=2 | 149 G → 3.35 G | 1 of 46 | 25.7 s → 0.9 s | 56.5 s → 36.6 s | 60 of 60 / 60 of 60 |
| `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`, 1 GPU | 61.3 G → 10.2 G | 3 of 14 | 10.1 s → 2.2 s | 22.8 s → 14.9 s | 59 of 61 / 59 of 61 |

Acceptance is a smoke check from one 120-token greedy completion per run, not an accuracy evaluation; the completions matched before and after.

A separate-repo drafter is unaffected: `zai-org/GLM-5.3` with `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark` on this branch loads the 2.3 G speculator in 0.5 s (total 116.9 s) and generates correctly.

For each opted-in head, the new rule was compared with the original filtering on every weight name of a real checkpoint (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.2-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-27B): zero mismatches. Scanning the 141 GLM-5.3 shard headers takes 0.12 s.

Tests and linters:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_filter_duplicate_safetensors.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_mm_encoder_only_weight_filter.py   # 51 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                      # passed
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>        # passed
```

Not validated:

- GLM-5.2 itself was not run end to end; GLM-5.3 uses the same `glm_moe_dsa` architecture and the same MTP head. From the published index, GLM-5.2 keeps 6 of 282 shards (29.9 of 1,403 GiB) and GLM-5.2-FP8 keeps 4 of 141 (20.0 of 704 GiB).
- The ROCm DeepSeek-V3.2 head has the same edit as the NVIDIA one but was not run on AMD hardware.
- Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next were not run end to end.
- Only InstantTensor was run end to end. The other safetensors load formats share the code path (the filter runs before the format is chosen) and are covered by the loader unit test only.

## Details

**Design.** A model may define `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name) -> bool`, returning True for checkpoint weights it does not load. `DefaultModelLoader` passes it through a new `Source.is_unused_weight` field, and `filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name` reads each shard's header and keeps only shards with at least one wanted tensor. Each opted-in head's `load_weights` calls the same rule, so the filter and the loader cannot drift apart. If the rule rejects every shard, the file list is left unchanged so the head's own missing-weight error still fires.

**Why shard level.** Whole-file loaders cannot skip single tensors, so the file list is the only lever vLLM has for them. MTP weights sit in a few shards, which is why this is enough.

**Relation to #58016 (not a duplicate).** #58016 adds an equivalent hook (`skip_checkpoint_weight`) and `Source` field but applies it per tensor inside `safetensors_weights_iterator`, which only helps the lazy safetensors path, and opts in only the DeepSeek-V4 DSpark drafter. This PR covers the whole-file loaders and the MTP heads. The two are complementary (drop shards, then skip tensors inside the kept ones), but the hooks are named differently, so whichever lands second should adopt the other's name and rebase the few shared lines in `default_loader.py`. Open PRs and issues were also searched for "MTP checkpoint load weights", "MTP shards skip", "draft model load entire checkpoint" and "MTP double load"; nothing else overlaps.

**Limitations.**

- Kept shards are still read in full. Qwen3.5 gains little: its head also loads `embed_tokens` and `lm_head`, which are spread across shards (Qwen3.5-27B keeps 5 of 11, Qwen3.5-9B keeps 4 of 4).
- Other MTP heads (DeepSeek V3, GLM-4, Kimi, Inkling, the ROCm/XPU V4 variants and others) are not opted in and behave as before.
- This does not help the EP weight filter under InstantTensor. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash, V4-Pro and Nemotron every shard holds at least one local expert at EP sizes 2, 4 and 8, so that needs per-tensor skipping inside InstantTensor itself.
- Loaders outside `DefaultModelLoader` (Run:ai streamer, tensorizer, sharded state, IPC weight cache) are untouched.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Respect Inductor deterministic mode in combo-kernel defaults
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

vLLM enables combo-kernel benchmarking by default, which conflicts with Inductor deterministic compilation and can fail a fresh Qwen3 startup in `may_ban_benchmarking`.

Disable automatic combo-kernel benchmarking when effective Inductor determinism is enabled. Preserve horizontal fusion, explicit combo settings, and CPU/version guards. Per-compile `deterministic` overrides the global setting; older Inductor configurations without that field retain existing defaults.

Relates to #58899. This addresses the startup conflict only. It does not address PyTorch's separate flag-restoration issue (pytorch/pytorch#198563) or guarantee reproducible serving output.

## Test Plan

- Extend `tests/compile/test_config.py` for global/per-compile precedence, explicit combo settings, platform/version guards, and missing Inductor setting.
- Compare original and patched configurations with fresh compiler caches on CUDA.
- Compare Qwen3-0.6B cold generation against the explicit workaround and a warm-cache restart, plus a normal-mode cold start.

## Test Result

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/compile/test_config.py -k combo_kernel -v`: original source **3 failed, 14 passed**; patched source **17 passed**.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/compile/test_config.py -k 'not test_VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE and not test_use_cudagraphs and not test_stock_torch_compile and not test_no_compilation and not test_enforce_eager and not test_torch_compile_disable' -v`: **83 passed, 11 deselected**. Model-fixture cases excluded from this run; small-model checks below are separate.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/config/compilation.py tests/compile/test_config.py docs/design/debug_vllm_compile.md`: passed applicable hooks.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual`: passed.
- Fresh CUDA q/k normalization compile: original defaults fail in combo benchmarking; patched defaults compile and match eager outputs at `rtol=atol=1e-5`.
- Qwen3-0.6B (`c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`), `custom_ops=['none']`, CUDA graphs disabled, greedy generation, three prompts × 16 tokens: original deterministic cold startup fails in `may_ban_benchmarking`; patched cold startup succeeds with 29 Inductor compilations. Tokens and all returned top-5 log probabilities exactly match the explicit `benchmark_combo_kernel=False` workaround and a warm-cache restart (0 recompilations). Normal-mode cold startup/generation also succeeds with 29 compilations.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04.4 WSL2, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 4050 Laptop GPU. Deterministic checks set `TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC=1`, `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` to keep the upstream flag-restoration issue separate. No performance claim or other-backend validation.

Duplicate checks found no open PR addressing this fix. #58918 was inspected and addresses a different compiler/cache change. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Rename AR speculators to StandaloneAR / TargetDependentAR
commits.pr_body:
`AutoRegressiveSpeculator` is the base class for EAGLE, MTP, and Gemma4. When `PlainDraftModelSpeculator` was added in #43091 to support vanilla draft-model speculation, the base-class name became misleading: both are autoregressive.

This PR renames them to make the actual distinction explicit:
- EAGLE, MTP, and Gemma4 are **target-dependent** autoregressive speculators. They consume target model state (hidden states, and for Gemma4 its KV cache). Thus, `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` was renamed to `TargetDependentARSpeculator`.
- The vanilla draft model is a **standalone** autoregressive speculator: it
  needs nothing from the target beyond the accepted/bonus token ids. This, `PlainDraftModelSpeculator` was renamed to `StandaloneARSpeculator`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix]Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: autotune(tuning_buckets=...) must round M up, not down (Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic with spec-decode)
commits.pr_body:
## Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` must map runtime M **up**, not down

Fixes the engine crash-loop at startup for SM100/SM103 block-scaled cute-dsl linear kernels (`mm_mxfp8` / `mm_fp4`) when speculative decoding is enabled.

### The crash

`kernel_warmup` runs dummy forwards inside `fi_utils.autotune(tuning_buckets=tuning_buckets)`. With spec-decode, the DSpark draft model forward runs at M = `max_num_seqs × k` = e.g. 8 × 3 = **24** — not a bucket value. Boot dies:

```
ValueError: Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
```

at `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py:5327` (`CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner.forward`), reached from the draft model's `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM.

Reproduced on DGX Station GB300 (SM103) with vLLM nightly + DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + dspark k=3; standalone FlashInfer-only repro at https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450.

### Root cause

`mm_mxfp8`'s own tuning config maps runtime M to buckets with `map_to_hybrid_bucket_uncapped`, which rounds **up**, and the cute-dsl split-K MMA tile is likewise chosen by rounding M up (`mma_tiler_mn_for_m`: 8/16/32). A tactic tuned at bucket b is therefore valid for every M ≤ b — tune space and apply space agree.

But inside `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` the autotuner **replaces the op's mapper** with `make_bucket_mapper(buckets, round_map=round_up)` and `round_up` **defaults to False** (floor). So the warmup dummy run at M=24 looks up the **bucket-16** tactic — tile (128,16), split_k=4 — and `forward()` rejects it because `mma_tiler_mn_for_m(24)` is (128,32).

Outside the context (serving, CUDA-graph capture) the op's own round-up mapper is restored, so **only the warmup pass ever crashes**: the engine can never boot, while the identical weights, tactics, and cache would serve fine.

Standalone repro (no vLLM, one process, same cache — all three regimes):

```
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=False [default]):
  M=24 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=12 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128,  8), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=40 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 32), (1, 1), True, False,  2)
outside any autotune context (op mapper, rounds up):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=True):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
```

### The fix

One line: `round_up=True` on the warmup `autotune()` call, making tune-context mapping equal serving-time mapping. Every cached tactic at bucket b is then applied only to M ≤ b — exactly the envelope both the split-K validator and the small swap-AB base tactics guarantee.

Profiling is per bucket, so tactic choices and the cache file are unchanged; only the dummy run's execution path changes. Verified live on GB300: the crash-looping boot (identical config) boots clean with this change and serves with full CUDA graphs; warmup passes on the pre-existing cache.

### Broader hazard (why this should land even before any FlashInfer-side change)

The base (non-split-K) candidate tactics include swap-AB tiles (128, 8/16/32) whose persistent-kernel `can_implement` requires `kernel_n ≤ tile_n` (kernel_n = token count in swap-AB) — and those tactics get **no apply-time check**. Under floor mapping, a bucket-16 winner applied at M=24 runs silently outside its envelope. The same tactic generator serves `mm_fp4`, so NVFP4 + spec-decode is exposed too. The split-K `ValueError` is just the one place that notices. Filed upstream with full analysis: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450

### Notes for reviewers

- The change is one argument on one line (plus the explanatory comment); the diff is intentionally minimal.
- If maintainers prefer the fix inside FlashInfer (honor the op's mapping direction under bucket override, or size small tiles against `DynamicDim.max`), this line remains a correct, self-contained fix on the vLLM side and can be revisited later.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Support NVFP4 KV cache on SM8x and SM12x with FlashInfer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` has a paged KV write path only on SM100, where trtllm-gen provides the native store, so the dtype cannot be used on SM8x or SM12x at all.

On SM8x and SM12x this writes the cache with FlashInfer's `nvfp4_quantize_append_paged_kv_cache_with_slot_mapping` and reads it back with the native fa2 prefill and decode wrappers, so no kernel change is needed. On SM12x, NVFP4 groups use the native decode wrapper instead of XQA and capture only single-token decode graphs, as on SM8x. One helper carves each page into its K and V halves for NHD and HND and leaves the data/scale split to the existing `nvfp4_split_data_scale`; SM100 builds its views through the same helper and keeps its trtllm-gen kernels. The query and output stay in model dtype on the fa2 path, so q_scale is not applied and no FP8 staging buffer is allocated. Both FlashInfer entry points are in the pinned 0.7.0, so no version bump is needed. On the sm_80 host used for validation, KV cache capacity went from 1,446,932 to 4,805,405 tokens (3.32x).

On these GPUs two combinations are refused in `supports_combination`, so the server stops at backend selection before the weights load: head_size 64, where fa2 prefill misreads NVFP4 by 10 to 15 percent once it picks the 128-row query tile (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5965, reproduced on sm_80 too), and attention sinks, since the sink prefill wrapper cannot read the block scales (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5966). flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6024 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6021 fix these but are not merged yet, so both refusals stay until the fixes ship in a FlashInfer release and the pin moves. DCP is refused in the metadata builder, because `supports_combination` does not see it. Scale-search variants such as `nvfp4_4over6` stay SM100-only because the slot-mapping writer has no scale search yet; once FlashInfer's writer supports it, enabling them here is a two- or three-line change.

`#46329`, `#54772` and `#56550` also target SM12x; this path needs no CUDA kernel or XQA change. RFC `#47684` tracks the wider work.

I used Codex and Claude while implementing and preparing this PR. I reviewed the final diff and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k nvfp4
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
vllm serve <Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B|Qwen/Qwen3-4B> --attention-backend FLASHINFER --kv-cache-dtype <auto|nvfp4> --max-model-len 4096 --port 8131
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 100 --port 8131
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --attention-backend FLASHINFER --kv-cache-dtype <auto|nvfp4> --max-model-len 128K --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --enable-chunked-prefill --reasoning-parser qwen3 --port 8099
python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py --port 8099 --num-samples 30 --needles 2 4 8 --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --seed 42 --concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

The GPU test writes through `do_kv_cache_update()` on all four block-compact layouts, dequantizes what the slot-mapping writer stored through the same views, and checks it against the input and that the neighbouring layer stays untouched. The read path is covered by the evals below. pre-commit passes.

mgoin ran this on SM121 with the stock `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` wheel; the results are in the comments. On sm_80 with the same stock wheel at `9adf229fb5`, the four nvfp4 tests pass, `openai/gpt-oss-20b` with an NVFP4 cache stops in 45 s with the head_size 64 reason, and GSM8K with the FLASHINFER backend for both dtypes gives:

| Model | Questions | bf16 KV | nvfp4 KV |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 100, two runs | 0.350, 0.350 | 0.170, 0.130 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | all 1319 | 0.384 | 0.174 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-4B (32 query / 8 KV heads) | 100, two runs | 0.920, 0.910 | 0.880, 0.880 |

MRCR on Qwen3.5-4B, 30 samples across needles 2/4/8 with prompts of 16,626 to 33,231 tokens, measured on an earlier, larger revision of this PR:

| KV dtype | Match ratio | Prefix hit rate | n2 | n4 | n8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| auto | 0.8523 | 1.0000 | 0.9949 | 0.7987 | 0.7633 |
| nvfp4 | 0.8452 | 0.9667 | 0.8951 | 0.8773 | 0.7633 |

SM100 now builds its views through the shared helper. For LBHNC and BLHNC, the two layouts SM100 accepts, they match the previous views on CPU whenever the cache has more than one block; SM100 itself was not run. SM86, SM89, SM120 and performance are untested.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Seed hybrid mamba state index with mamba_block_size on prefix-cache hits
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix an out-of-bounds read on prefix-cache hits for hybrid mamba models whose KV config contains a prefix-cacheable attention group with a block size smaller than `mamba_block_size` (e.g. a DFlash2/EAGLE sliding-window drafter group with block 64).

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot with `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`. By then `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has reassigned `cache_config.block_size = min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`, so on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA + sparse MLA, mamba block 7168, drafter block 64/1024) the seed is in the wrong units. `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` takes it as `src_col` and `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`): cached prefixes of ≥ 8 mamba blocks fault (`Xid 31`, `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync), shorter hits silently restore the wrong recurrent state.

The fix divides by `cache_config.mamba_block_size`, the unit used for mamba blocks everywhere else (`MambaSpec.block_size`, the preprocess kernel, the block-table width; `mamba_attn.py` already derives the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`).

Fixes #55600.

## Test Plan

No unit test is included; the failure needs a hybrid model whose KV groups include a smaller-block prefix-cacheable group. Manual verification on GLM-5.3-Flash (EXL3, TP=1, DFlash2 `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `max_num_seqs=1`) on a DGX Spark, before/after on identical inputs.

## Test Result

- Prompt A = 57 344 tokens (8 full mamba blocks), then A + a different question: before → HTTP 500 in 0.2 s, `NVRM: Xid 31 ... FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`; after → completes in 11.7 s with 50 176 cached tokens.
- After: 13-, 34- and 63-block prefix hits complete; multi-needle recall on warm (cached) requests equals cold at 100k / 250k / 450k tokens (5/5 each); warm TTFT 8.7 s vs 139 s cold at 100k.
- 3-hour soak (57 multi-turn conversation turns with a prefix hit on every turn, contexts up to 184k tokens, fresh 41k–354k-token prompts): 133/133 requests OK, zero faults.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Triton] Migrating MiniMax-M3 kernels from make_block_ptr to tensor descriptors
commits.pr_body:
Replace the deprecated tl.make_block_ptr API with tl.make_tensor_descriptor in the MiniMax-M3 sparse attention and index top-k Triton kernels.

**Summary:** GSM8K matches upstream within stderr. Across 1k/4k/8k at c=1/32/64, mean TPOT, ITL, E2EL and output throughput are within ±1.9% of upstream main.

## MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on ROCm: test results (2026-10-01)

Environment

| Component | Installed | `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pin | Match |
|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `danichan/triton_api_deprecation` @ `d30488a7a5` (ROCm/vllm), built from source; upstream = the three files at main `17e9295dd5` | — | — |
| Triton | `Triton 3.8.0+git669b31ac` | `TRITON_BRANCH="669b31a"` (release/internal/3.8.x) | ✅ |
| aiter | `amd-aiter 0.1.23` | `AITER_BRANCH="v0.1.23"` | ✅ |
| PyTorch | `torch 2.13.0+git733fca1` | `PYTORCH_BRANCH="733fca1"` | ✅ |

Server

```bash
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve /data/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --port 8000 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
commits.pr_body:
## Summary
Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation, the prefill
(producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead blocks that the
decode (consumer) side never allocates. The producer's local block list therefore ends up
**longer** than the consumer's remote list, and the first prefill→decode KV write crashed
with `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` (e.g. 8003 vs 8000 at n=3),
making MTP unusable on MoRI-IO.

## Fix
The surplus is trailing lookahead scratch, not prompt KV, so it must be dropped **before**
the producer saves — not masked at transfer time.

- **Clamp on the WRITE producer save path** (`MoRIIOConnectorScheduler`): a new
  `_clamp_to_prompt_blocks` trims each **full-attention** KV group to its prompt length
  (`ceil(num_prompt_tokens / block_size)`), block-size-agnostic and per-group so it works
  under the hybrid multi-KV-group manager. Sliding-window groups are left untouched.
- **Chunked-prefill final-chunk detection by token progress** (`_is_final_prefill_chunk`):
  the save fires when `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled >= num_prompt_tokens`, which is
  immune to speculative-lookahead block inflation (a block-count check is not). This also
  correctly handles a final chunk that allocates **no new blocks** (`new_block_ids is None`),
  which previously dropped the save and hung the decode leg.
- **Keep the loud invariant**: `compute_block_transfer_offsets` still raises on a genuinely
  longer-local list — a real bug in READ mode — rather than silently clamping. The relaxation
  lives only in the WRITE save path where the surplus is legitimate.
- **Fail closed on unsupported combos**: MoRI-IO WRITE mode + sliding-window attention (with
  or without spec decode) raises `NotImplementedError`, because the positional prompt-prefix
  save would ship out-of-window null blocks. READ + SWA (+ spec) is unaffected: block ids are
  pre-clipped to computed tokens before the connector sees them.

## Tests
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py`: WRITE-mode clamp (single- and
  multi-group), chunked-prefill accumulation, the lookahead final-chunk regression (final
  chunk with `new_block_ids=None`), and the WRITE spec+SWA guard (reachable only under a
  uniform SWA model with `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py`: retains the loud longer-local
  `ValueError` guard and the shorter-local READ-mode partial-transfer behavior.

## Validation
GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP **1P1D / 1P2D PD-disagg** (vLLM v0.27.1 + AITER v0.1.19), MTP n=3:
- KV transfer succeeds (clamp fires, e.g. `8003 -> 8000` / `8 -> 5`); no more ValueError.
- Coherent output, **0 token-0 (`!`) corruption**, FULL cudagraph engaged.
- 8k/8k decode-heavy shows the expected MTP TPOT win (1.36–1.45×) at low concurrency.

## Not a duplicate
This is the only open PR addressing MoRI-IO KV block-offset handling under speculative
decoding. It builds on (does not duplicate) the upstream hybrid/multi-KV-group MoRI-IO
refactor: it keeps that connector's structure and guards, and only adds the spec-decode
clamp + lookahead-safe final-chunk detection on top.

## AI assistance
Prepared with AI assistance (Cursor). All changed lines and tests were reviewed, and the
behavior was validated end-to-end by the submitter on GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP PD-disaggregated
serving (1P1D/1P2D).

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py` (ROCm + mori) — 62 passed
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean
- [x] MoRI-IO PD-disagg smoke with `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` on both roles
- [x] Non-spec PD-disagg regression (equal local/remote path unchanged)

commits.pr_title: [XPU][MoE] Tune Triton fused MoE for Intel XPU
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Triton fused MoE kernel runs on Intel XPU but had no tuned configs, so it
always fell back to `get_default_config()`. This PR enables XPU tuning in
`benchmark_moe.py` and adds Intel Arc Pro B70 configs.

## Changes

- Add an XPU tuning search space and prune `BLOCK_SIZE_M` by rows routed
  per expert, guarded by `current_platform.is_xpu()`.
- Preserve XPU's `grf_mode` in serialized configs.
- Use `current_platform.device_type` as the worker's default device and
  pick `torch.xpu.XPUGraph` on XPU, capturing through
  `current_platform.graph()` (as `benchmark_selective_state_update.py`
  does); these are the only CUDA-specific calls that block XPU.
- Ship `E=64,N=1024`, `E=64,N=512`, and `E=128,N=384` configs. The other
  shapes below are additional validation and are not in this revision.

The Ray path is unchanged. On XPU, Ray registers the `"GPU"` resource only
when `dpctl` is installed, and tuning should run on one card
(`ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=<id>`): with several cards visible, the per-worker
`ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` Ray sets arrives after Level Zero is initialized, so all
workers end up on device 0.

## Results

Intel Arc Pro B70, bf16. Baseline is Triton's built-in heuristic; tuned uses
the generated JSON. Full per-batch sweeps (18 sizes) are available for the
three shapes below; geometric-mean speedups are 1.86x (`E=64,N=1024`),
1.91x (`E=64,N=512`), and 1.92x (`E=60,N=1408`).

| batch | OLMoE E=64,N=1024 tp=1 | OLMoE E=64,N=512 tp=2 | Qwen1.5-MoE E=60,N=1408 tp=1 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.41x | 1.21x | 1.23x |
| 8 | 1.75x | — | 1.79x |
| 32 | 1.81x | — | 1.85x |
| 128 | 3.02x | 2.78x | 3.11x |
| 512 | 1.44x | 1.39x | 1.33x |
| 2048 | 2.82x | 2.59x | 3.36x |
| 4096 | 2.65x | 2.36x | 2.98x |

(Full 18-row sweeps per shape available on request.)

`E=64,N=704` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite) and `E=128,N=384` (Qwen3-30B-A3B /
Qwen3-Coder tp=2) passed fp32-reference validation (rel_l2 ~4.1e-3) but
per-batch kernel numbers were not retained; only aggregate/e2e results are
reported for them below.

At tp=4, Qwen3-Coder's local shape is `E=128,N=192` (not shipped in this
revision): all 18 tuned configs passed fp32 validation
(`rel_l2=3.82e-3..4.20e-3`), with microkernel latency down 43.73% mean /
43.34% median vs the heuristic (aggregate only, no per-batch table).

### End-to-end

All rows use explicit `--moe-backend triton`, comparing Triton's built-in
heuristic (baseline) with the tuned shape-specific JSON config. Workload is
512 input tokens, 128 output tokens, 32 prompts, unless noted otherwise:

| model | shape | TP | baseline | tuned | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | `E=64,N=1024` | 1 | 3022.8 tok/s | 4146.4 tok/s | 1.37x |
| `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | `E=64,N=512` | 2 | 2731.8 tok/s | 3084.2 tok/s | 1.13x |
| `Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B` | `E=60,N=1408` | 1 | 652.5 tok/s | 697.9 tok/s | 1.070x |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` | `E=64,N=704` | 2 | 739.1 tok/s | 756.4 tok/s | 1.023x |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct` | `E=128,N=192` | 4 | 1980.3 tok/s | 2061.1 tok/s | 1.041x |

Qwen1.5-MoE used 12 samples/arm (p=7.4e-07); DeepSeek used 4 samples/arm
(p=0.0022); Qwen3-Coder used 6 samples/arm, balanced order, fresh engines
(+4.10% mean, 95% bootstrap CI [+3.09%, +5.88%]).

## Test plan

- Tune on XPU with `pip install dpctl`, then
  `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0 python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model <model> --tp-size <tp> --tune`.
- Verify every generated winner against an fp32 reference.
- Confirm serving with `--moe-backend triton` loads the exact JSON.
- Compare heuristic and tuned Triton with identical workloads and fresh engines.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean. CUDA/ROCm keep
  `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` and `torch.cuda.graph`; not run on CUDA/ROCm.
